### Amendment 179 — the localStorage save store is DRIVABLE: storage becomes a seam, and the durable lie is refused (2026-10-07)

**What landed.** M5's v170 open item closed: `createLocalStorageSaveStore` had ZERO coverage because it
reached for `window.localStorage` directly, so it could not even be CONSTRUCTED outside a browser tab.
v179 makes the storage an injected seam — `options.storage` (the minimal `StorageLike`:
`getItem`/`setItem`/`removeItem`, deliberately NOT the full `Storage` interface, since the index gives
`list()` its names and no key-enumeration is needed) drives the SAME code headlessly, and the no-option
default keeps probing `window.localStorage`, so the Studio consumer (`Scene3D`, `nexus-save:studio-scene`)
is unchanged byte for byte. The seam's first tests caught one real lie in the store itself:
`writeAtomic`'s `durable` argument was silently IGNORED — the memory store refuses it outright and the
fs store checks for `flushSync` before writing; now this store refuses it too, and the refusal is tested
with the zero-write guarantee its siblings' tests pin.

**Measured.** `@nexus/three-runtime` 422 → **436** tests (+14 in the new `test/saveLocalStorage.test.ts`):
headless construction with an injected storage, byte-for-byte round-trips (a miss reads as null, never
empty), index-driven listing sorted with no `__index` key named and no debris, namespace isolation over
ONE backing storage (keys carry the namespace; an emptied index key remains by design), the
creation-only temp-suffix rule (refused to CREATE, readable as a leftover the host already holds),
refusal classification without reading any bytes, a writeAtomic round-trip leaving NO temp key behind,
the durable refusal with zero bytes written (and the store still works right after), a mid-flight quota
failure cleaning up its temp and writing nothing to the target, a corrupt index answered honestly
(`[]`, and non-string names type-filtered), and a rename moving bytes and index together. tsc clean;
`tools/harness/studio-scene3d.mjs` **25/25** in a REAL browser — the unchanged default path still saves
and loads across the surface.

**Bounds (§60).** The seam changes nothing about WHERE saves live: still per-origin, ~5MB-capped,
unauthenticated browser localStorage — hosted persistence remains M7 (ADR 0014 stays the local-first
story). The emptied `__index` key stays on file by design. The durable refusal is a capability
statement the Studio cannot observe today (nothing passes `durable`); when a consumer needs durability
it needs a different host, not a softer promise here.

### Amendment 180 — M5: a quota refusal is NAMED, not quoted raw (localStorage store), and the save note stops lying about disk (2026-10-07)

**What landed.** Two sentences the product owed its user, both paid:

1. `saveStore.ts` — the localStorage store's three data-writing verbs (`write`, `writeAtomic`'s temp step,
   `rename`) now catch a quota-SHAPED `setItem` throw and re-throw a sentence that names the quota AND the
   fact that nothing was written (`the origin's quota is full and NOTHING was written; delete saves and
   retry, or clear this origin`), with the original storage words riding along. Any error the store cannot
   classify is re-thrown untouched — no invented diagnosis (§60). The mid-flight sentence of v179 keeps
   ownership of the copy-step failure, where the temp already exists.
2. `Scene3D.tsx` — the save note no longer says "nothing written to disk" (v163 text, true only before the
   localStorage backend of v170 existed): it now says `persisted in this origin's localStorage
   (reload-safe), not on disk`. The browser harness pinned `includes('saved 5 bodies')`, which the honest
   suffix keeps matching.

**Measured.** three-runtime 436 → **440** (+4: write quota + zero-write, temp-step quota vs mid-flight
ownership, unclassifiable error re-thrown untouched, rename quota with the OLD save surviving); studio
**256/256** regression; `npm run build` (tsc) clean; harness studio-scene3d **25/25** against the real
default path.

**Bounds (§60).** The quota detection is shape-based (`/quota/i` or `/exceed/i` over name+message) because
engine messages vary; a private-mode `SecurityError` is NOT quota-shaped and stays raw. The
index-update-fails path (target bytes written, index stale) is still raw — the write surfaces a
quota-named throw only when the DATA write refuses. The Studio save dialog has no quota meter; the
browse UI's delete buttons (v169/171) are the remedy the note names.
### Amendment 181 — M5: the 3D surface PANS — the camera rig slides across the ground, by shift-drag and by keyboard (2026-10-07)

**What landed.** The first of M5's "still open" controls, built the way v161 built the orbit — pure
arithmetic first, the component only forwarding input:

1. `scene3d.ts` — `OrbitState` gains `panX`/`panZ`: world-unit offsets that slide the orbit TARGET along
   the ground plane. New `applyPan` converts CAMERA-relative deltas (`forward`, `right`) with the azimuth
   the orbit already holds — forward is `(−sin az, 0, −cos az)`, right is `(cos az, 0, −sin az)` — so a
   key means "into the screen", not "−Z". Each axis clamps independently at `±ORBIT_PAN_LIMIT` (12 world
   units); `applyOrbit` rides the offsets through untouched (turning never moves what the camera looks
   at); `orbitToPlacement` slides the whole rig (`lookAt = anchor + pan`, `position = anchor + pan +
   spherical`) so a pan changes neither the turn nor the reach; `orbitFromPlacement` answers pan zero by
   definition. Pan is HORIZONTAL-ONLY by declaration — a vertical target would fight the elevation clamp,
   and an undeclared axis that silently did nothing would be a control that lies. The surface grows one
   verb, `panBy({forward?, right?})`; `resetOrbit` clears the pan because the default carries none.
2. `Scene3D.tsx` — SHIFT-drag grabs the ground (the world follows the cursor, so the target moves
   opposite the drag); WASD and the arrow keys walk camera-relatively (W into the screen, S out, A/D
   sideways). The keydown listener is its own effect with its own cleanup, and a key aimed at an
   input/textarea/select/contentEditable is ignored — typing in the agent panel is not camera input. The
   HUD's orbit line reports the pan alongside az/el/distance.

**Measured.** studio 256 → **263** (+7 pan cases in `scene3d.test.ts`: the camera-relative conversion at
two azimuths, independent per-axis clamps, `orbitBy` preserving pan, the rig-wide `orbitToPlacement`, the
default carrying none, `surface.panBy` through the adapter, `resetOrbit` clearing it); `npm run build`
clean; harness studio-scene3d 25 → **30/30** in a real browser — W pans `0/0 → −1.097/−1.672`, D strafes,
reset clears, and shift-drag moves the pan while the azimuth sits frozen at 0.581 (pan moved + azimuth
frozen is a pan; an orbit wearing this one's name would have turned).

**Bounds (§60).** Pan is horizontal-only: Y never pans. The keyboard listener consumes WASD/arrows
page-wide (scoped by the input guard, not by focus), so a surface that wanted its own key map inside a
page with other key consumers would need a narrower rule. The pan limit is a constant, not a setting;
there is no pan inertia, no held-key interpolation, and no pan meter in the HUD beyond the two numbers
the report already prints.
### Amendment 182 — M5: the surface NAMES what a click touches — the per-body picker (2026-10-07)

**What landed.** The second of M5's "still open" controls, built the way v161 built the orbit and
v181 the pan — the geometry lives in the runtime, the arithmetic lives in the lib, the component
only forwards input:

1. `three-runtime` — new `pickAt(sceneId, nx, ny): ScenePick | null`. NDC in (y points UP, the
   convention `ndcFromPixel` converts to), a `ScenePick` out: `{ entityId, name, distance }`. The
   ray is a real `THREE.Raycaster.setFromCamera` into the LIVE scene — `updateMatrixWorld(true)`
   first, so the answer describes the scene AS IT STANDS, not as the last frame left it (a pick
   after a drag must not answer with yesterday's matrices). Invisible bodies are skipped, the
   nearest hit across entities wins (distance is along the pick ray, so an overlap names the closer
   body), no active camera answers `null`, and a missing scene throws the way every other lookup
   does.
2. `scene3d.ts` — `ndcFromPixel(px, py, w, h)` is pure arithmetic with ONE non-obvious detail: y is
   written `1 − (py/h)·2`, not `−((py/h)·2 − 1)` — the second form produces `-0` at the center, and
   deep-equal distinguishes `-0` from `0`. The report gains `selected: { id, name } | null` (the
   SURFACE holds it, the way it holds the orbit), and the surface grows `pickAt(px, py)`: no adapter
   pick or no backend dimensions is an honest NO-OP that answers the unchanged report — asking
   nothing is not the same answer as picking nothing.
3. `Scene3D.tsx` — the adapter forwards to the runtime; a pointer release within
   `PICK_MAX_CLICK_PIXELS` (4) of its press is a CLICK and picks (anything farther was a drag, and
   drags only move the camera); pointerCancel clears both refs; the HUD carries a `picked:` line
   that shows the name or an honest `—` when the sky was clicked.

**Measured.** three-runtime 440 → **448** (+8: center hit, corner sky, near-beats-far, invisible is
unpickable, no camera, unknown scene throws, the pick follows the LIVE scene both ways — a body
moved away unpicks and a re-aimed camera re-picks — and the NDC y-up convention pinned at ±0.26);
studio 263 → **274** (+4 `ndcFromPixel` cases including the −0 trap, +6 pure pick cases through the
fake adapter, +1 end-to-end on the REAL runtime: the view center names Cube B, the corner answers
null); `npm run build` clean; harness studio-scene3d 30 → **33/33** in a real browser — a pinned
click names Cube A and the HUD agrees, a second pinned click names Cube C (DIFFERENT: the pick is
spatial, not a constant), and empty sky clears the selection with the HUD answering `picked: —`.

**The center-pin decision.** The probe (`.scratch/v182/probe-pick.mjs`) measured the demo view: the
pixel at the exact center names Cube B with a margin of only ~0.16 world units, because the demo's
frame loop drifts every body's y by `bob·0.01` PER FRAME — an unbounded random walk in a
long-running page. So the BROWSER assertion pins Cube A and Cube C (whose margins are the whole
half-box, ~0.5) plus spatial discrimination, and the exact center answer is pinned in
`scene3dSurface.test.ts`, where no frame loop runs and the ray is deterministic.

**Bounds (§60).** A pick NAMES a body; it does not yet DO anything to it — no highlight, no
inspector, no edit semantics ride on `selected` yet. The 4 px threshold is a constant, not a
setting. The pick answers the nearest VISIBLE entity only — occlusion by invisible geometry is not
modeled, and cameras, lights and helpers are not pickable, only bodies.

### Amendment 183 — the lighting is CONTROLLABLE (M5 v183)

`createScene` attached two lights (v142) and nothing in the package could touch them again: the
lighting was write-once, so a "lighting control" above the package had nothing to call. v183 adds
the gate, and the Studio becomes its first consumer.

**Runtime.** `ThreeRuntime.setLightState(sceneId, lightId, { enabled?, intensity? }): boolean` —
the one method that changes a declared light. It upholds v142's rule THROUGH the gate: toggling
`enabled` attaches and detaches the wrapped `THREE.Light` (a control that flipped a config field
alone would describe a darkness the renderer never renders). An illegal intensity (non-finite or
negative) refuses the WHOLE change — nothing half-applies — and an unknown scene or light answers
`false`, the same report `removeEntity` gives. Light ids are SCENE-LOCAL names (`ambient`,
`directional` in every scene), not global brands: the gate resolves against the scene it was
handed, and a sibling scene holding the same-named light is untouched.

**Studio (pure).** `clampLightIntensity` folds any ask into `LIGHT_INTENSITY_MIN..MAX` (0..2 — the
demo opens at 0.5 and 1.0, so the range covers "off-black" through "twice the sun"); one rule for
every non-finite number, +Infinity included: a brightness that is not a number means "off". The
surface clamps BEFORE the host sees the ask, so the runtime's own refusal is a second wall, never
the first. `lightIntensityOf` is the one reader that knows both host shapes — the real runtime
keeps brightness on the wrapped three.js object, a structural fake may keep it directly; a light
that declares neither reads 0 rather than inventing a value. `SceneReport.scene.lighting` is the
scene's lights as the LIVE scene holds them (never a shadow the surface keeps — a change goes
through the gate and the next report re-reads what the host now holds), and a host without a gate
answers the unchanged report: asking is not changing.

**Surface.** `setLight(lightId, { enabled?, intensity? })` — clamps, hands the rest to the host's
gate, returns the re-read report.

**Face.** The HUD lists each declared light with an on/off toggle and −/+ brightness buttons
(one press = `LIGHT_INTENSITY_STEP` = 0.1, clamped at both ends). The numbers are the report's, so
a press that moved only local state would show nothing — and the honest text for a gate-less host
is its unchanged lights.

**Verification.** three-runtime 448 → **453** (+5: live-write vs config-shadow, detach/re-attach,
whole-change refusal, unknown light/scene, scene-local ids); studio 274 → **283** (+8 pure-surface
cases incl. the range fold and the unchanged-report guarantee, +1 end-to-end on the shipped
headless runtime: surface ask → runtime gate → live light → honest report); tsc/lint/build clean;
harness studio-scene3d 33 → **37/37** — the toggle, the dim (1.00 → 0.90) and the re-enable are
pressed BY HAND in a real browser, each read back through the bridge.

**A build found a second defect, not in the diff.** First harness run: the HUD buttons rendered,
the click landed, and the runtime did not change. The cause: `transpilePackages` compiles the
shared packages, but module RESOLUTION still follows `main` — the Studio's browser bundle runs
`packages/three-runtime/dist`, and dist was v182. The new method did not exist there, and the
surface's optional call silently skipped it. The unit suites never saw this: they import the
package through vitest's source mapping. Rule the incident pins: **changing `packages/*/src`
requires rebuilding that package before any browser-facing check is meaningful.**

**Bounds (§60).** The control changes enabled and intensity; it does not create or delete lights,
move them, or touch colour — the demo's two declared lights are what it names. There is no
persistent lighting state: a save file still records nothing about a light the person dimmed.


## Amendment 184 — the save REALLY persists: store AND disk (M5 v184)

v163-v180's save note said "persisted in this origin's localStorage" and it was a LIE the whole
time: `surface.save()` only BUILT the runtime's file, nothing in the product face ever called
`writeSaveFile`, and the store stayed empty through every green run - the harness checked the
note and the in-memory round trip, never the store, so 37/37 kept passing over an unbuilt claim.
v184 closes the lie and spends the runtime's oldest waiting capability: the fs-backed SaveStore
of v120 finally gets a product consumer.

**Studio (the store write).** `onSave` now calls `runtime.writeSaveFile('last-saved', ...)` and
the note carries the write report's OWN byte count (`2307 bytes in this origin's localStorage
('last-saved', reload-safe), not on disk`) - every number on screen is the store's receipt, and a
refusing store (quota) fails the save loudly instead of quietly keeping the file to itself.

**Studio (server).** `saveFsServer.ts` + `app/api/agent/save-fs` (route, nodejs): the route
speaks exactly two actions (`write`, `read`) plus a GET probe. The store is the runtime's OWN
`createFsSaveStore` over node:fs injected as `FsLike` (`nodeSaveFs` - its `writeFileSync` mkdirs
the parent first, and it deliberately offers no `flushSync`, so a `durable` ask is refused by the
store's own sentence rather than downgraded). The naming rules stay the store's - no absolute
forms, no `..`, no backslash, no temp suffix on creation - and every refusal crosses as
`ok:false` plus the store's sentence, paraphrased by nobody. A non-object file is refused BEFORE
any byte moves (the v163 door rule, one seam over); a read tells missing, not-JSON and
parses-but-not-an-object apart by name. Saves land in `.nexus/scene-saves` (gitignored since
v177, beside the deploy records).

**Studio (lane + face).** `saveFsLane.ts` is a fetch adapter importing nothing from the runtime
or the server module (types re-stated locally); the HUD grows `save to disk` (one save, two named
destinations - the store and the disk get the same bytes), `browse disk` (names only - a listing
is a fact about names, not bytes), and disk rows that load a save into a FRESH scene through the
same non-overwriting `surface.load`.

**Harness.** 37 -> **42**: the store's own browse verb now lists what save wrote (the lie's
direct counter-proof), `save to disk` answers with path + bytes, the file is read back OFF DISK
with node:fs and parses to the runtime's format (5 bodies), the disk row lists, and clicking it
round-trips through the real disk into a fresh scene. The run also caught a real regression of
its own: the HUD panel had grown wide enough to cover the canvas center, so drags and picks
aimed at the scene landed on the panel's clickable rows instead - the press point moved to the
lower-right quadrant and the panel got a max width, because a HUD that swallows input meant for
the scene it describes is a HUD gone wrong.

**Verification.** studio 283 -> **297** (+14: 7 server over a memFs fake + a REAL tmpdir round
trip proving `nodeSaveFs` lands bytes on disk through a nested root, 7 lane over a stubbed
fetch); tsc clean via `next build`, lint clean at `--max-warnings=0`, harness **42/42** with
`backend=webgl`; the disk file's bytes are asserted from OUTSIDE the page (node:fs), so a write
that only claimed to happen would fail twice - in the route answer and in the file read.

**Bounds (§60).** One fixed save name (`last-saved`) per store; the disk store holds what the
route wrote and nothing browses sub-directories differently; no disk delete or rename from the
panel (the store supports both; the face does not expose them yet); no quota meter; `durable`
is refused, not downgraded; and a save on disk is a file on THIS server - not a publish, not a
backup, not a cloud.

## Amendment 185 — the save area METERERS what it holds (M5 v185)

v180 taught the store to refuse a full quota with a sentence; nothing above it showed the numbers
that sentence is about. The save dialog asked for a quota meter, and the honest version of one
measures instead of guessing. Two figures, each owned by whoever can actually measure it:

**The store's own footprint.** `list()` still reads no bytes - that rule stands, because a menu
that costs O(total bytes) is the wrong seam. The meter is the CALLER that pays the cost on
purpose: the decorated listing (v169) already reads each save to show its header, and it now
carries the file's `chars` with it; `footprintOf` sums what was measured. The unit is CHARS, not
bytes - the figure is a JS string's `length` (UTF-16 code units), the same unit localStorage
quotas are counted in, and "bytes" would be a claim about encodings this code does not make.
An entry whose read failed stays in the save count and contributes nothing to the total - a
meter that invented a size would be a lie with digits.

**The origin's usage.** `navigator.storage.estimate()` is the browser's own answer, and it covers
EVERY storage API on the origin, not just localStorage - the label says so. The adapter is a
structural slice of `navigator` (`StorageEstimateHost`), half-answered estimates keep their
unknown half ("quota unknown"), a missing estimate or a throwing one answers "the browser
exposes no storage estimate here", and a percent is only computed when both halves are numeric
and the quota is not zero - a percent that cannot be computed is not computed (§60).

**Face.** The save area grows a meter block: the store line (`1 save · 2311 chars in
'studio-scene'`), the origin line with its honesty tag (`browser estimate, all storage APIs`),
and a 4px bar whose width is the percent (a 0.5% floor so a near-empty origin still shows a
sliver). The meter re-MEASURES after every store mutation - save, save-to-disk, delete, rename,
browse - never arithmetic-ing a delta the store can answer directly.

**Verification.** studio 297 -> **318** (+21: footprint/format/bytes/estimate-adapter/percent/
origin-sentence, including a half-answered estimate and a throwing one); tsc clean, lint clean
at `--max-warnings=0`, `next build` clean, harness **46/46** (`backend=webgl`) - the meter reads
`1 save · 2311 chars` after the store write, the origin line carries the browser's 10.0 GB
estimate, the bar renders, and DELETING the save re-measures the meter to `0 saves · 0 chars`.

**Bounds (§60).** The meter reports what it measured and what the browser estimated - it does not
predict when the quota will fill, it does not poll (a re-read happens on mutation, not on a
timer), and the chars figure is this build's own measure of its namespace, not the origin total.

## Amendment 186 — the disk rows are MANAGEABLE: delete and rename reach the server's real file (M5 v186)

M5's open list closed at v185 with one entry still parked in the v184 bounds: the disk rows could be
listed and loaded, but the verbs the store rows have had since v172 — delete and rename — stopped at
the store boundary. The runtime's fs-backed SaveStore has answered those verbs all along (`delete`
returns the store's own boolean, `rename` resolves the new name through the creation rule); only the
product face was missing. v186 wires the face, and every naming rule stays the store's.

- **Server** (`saveFsServer.ts`): `deleteStudioSceneSave` and `renameStudioSceneSave`. A non-string
  path is refused here (one sentence per missing half); everything else is the store's own answer —
  `delete` passes the boolean through ("already gone" is `ok: true, deleted: false`, not an error),
  and `rename` refuses a missing OLD name with the store's sentence while the NEW name goes through
  the store's creation rule (`resolveNewSavePath`: no absolute forms, no `..`, no temp-suffix
  collision). This module paraphrases nobody.
- **Route** (`app/api/agent/save-fs`): the POST action whitelist grows from `write | read` to
  `write | read | delete | rename`; dispatch only. Refusals stay honest answers (`ok: false`), 400s.
- **Lane** (`saveFsLane.ts`): `deleteSaveOnDisk` and `renameSaveOnDisk` — fetch adapters, still
  importing nothing from the runtime. Unreachability is an answer, as in v184.
- **Panel** (`Scene3D.tsx`): each disk row carries delete/rename buttons (`data-scene3d-disk-delete`
  / `data-scene3d-disk-rename`), `stopPropagation` so the row's click-to-load never fires beneath
  them. After either verb the rows are RE-PROBED, not hand-edited — what the panel lists stays a
  fact about the disk. The rename prompt is the browser's own; the new name is a server-side
  creation and is validated there.
- **Harness** (studio-scene3d.mjs, 46 → 53): rename through the panel (`prompt` overridden in the
  page), the file's move read back with node:fs (old gone, new present), rows following the rename,
  delete through the panel, absence proven on the real disk, rows following the delete. The disk
  baseline is swept before launch — a renamed leftover would otherwise stand between the facts and
  the run. Two probes learned the harness's own rule again: a `waitForFunction` predicate that
  always returns an object never waits (first `{"gone":false,"here":false}` was the probe's timing,
  not the panel's); predicates now return null until the fact they name holds.

Bounds retired from v184's list: "no disk delete or rename from the panel". Bounds that remain:
one fixed save name per store; no quota-fill prediction and no polling.

Tests: studio 327/327 (saveFsServer 12, saveFsLane 11 — nine new), three-runtime untouched at
453/453, harness 53/53 (backend=webgl). tsc, eslint, next build clean.

### Amendment 187 (M3 v187, studio) — the Assets surface can ask for FOOTAGE: the type crosses to the generator untouched, and the panel's dispatch is what keeps a still from being stored under a video ask

_Numbering: 187 was free (`grep -ao "^### Amendment 1[0-9][0-9]"` topped out at 186). Full narrative in
`docs/evidence/studio/README.md`; this is the ledger entry._

- **The gap this closes.** The plan listed video generation as having **no product surface** — the agent door
  `asset.video.generate` existed since v160, and nothing in the Studio could reach it. `generateAsset` gains
  a `type: 'image' | 'video'` (defaulting to `'image'`, so every existing caller is unchanged) and the panel
  gains an image/video toggle.
- **The defect the dispatch prevents, MEASURED rather than asserted.** Both demo generators answer whatever
  they are asked: `DemoImageGenerator.generate({ type: 'video', … })` returns an **`image/png`**. So a panel
  holding ONE generator would store a still under a video ask and label it footage. The proof measures that
  first (§6a prints `image/png`), then shows the fix (§6b: the ask reaches the video generator and comes back
  `video/mp4`). The dispatch lives in the panel, where the real classes are touched — `lib/assets.ts` never
  inspects the type, it forwards it.
- **The type in the report is the GENERATOR's, not this module's.** `generateAsset` does not stamp
  `'video'` on the result; what the generator answered is what the library stores, and `buildAssetReport`
  reads back the metadata the library holds. A module that relabelled would make the proof's
  `type === 'video'` check pass against its own label instead of against the package.
- **A still and footage are told apart by a `null`, not a zero.** `AssetSummary` gains `duration: number |
  null`: footage reports the seconds it was made for, a still reports **`null`** — because `0` would claim a
  still is a zero-length video. The proof asserts both sides of that.
- **§60 holds on the video write.** The footage stores **0 bytes** and the library's `storedBytes` stays 0 —
  DEMO MODE has no footage any more than it has pixels — and the panel still renders **no `<img>`**, checked
  in the browser against the DOM. The surface's mode line now says *"no image **or video** model is
  attached"*.
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/assets.test.ts` **14 → 24 cases** (the video block: the type reaches the generator,
  footage reports a duration, a still reports null, the payload is still empty, and the default stays
  `'image'` for an untyped call); `asset-surface-proof.mjs` gains **§6a/§6b** over the REAL generators;
  `tools/harness/studio-assets.mjs` — the REAL browser, **24/24 → 29/29**: the probe clicks the video
  toggle, types, presses Generate, waits for the count to rise, and checks the new asset is `video/mp4` with
  a positive duration and zero bytes. apps/studio **201 → 332** (27 files), `tsc` clean.
- **Bounds (§60).** The surface can now ASK for footage; it cannot play it, scrub it, or see it — there is no
  video element anywhere, because there is no video. `asset.video.generate`'s agent door and this surface
  both exist now, and they agree on what the type means. Character consistency still has no product surface,
  and there is still no asset UPDATE or storyboard editing.
## Amendment 188 — the board is EDITABLE: remove and reorder reach the storyboard manager (M3 v188)

M3's open list shrank to three at v187, and all three had the same shape as the video ask did: the
package has answered the verb for versions, only the Studio product face was missing. v188 takes the
first of them — storyboard editing. `StoryboardManager` has had `removeFrame` (splice, survivors keep
their `order`) and `reorderFrames` (full-sequence resequencing, `order` rewritten 0..n-1) since v91;
since v153 the Studio's Assets surface has READ the board. Now it can edit it, and every rule stays
the manager's.

- **Pure layer** (`assets.ts`): `removeStoryboardFrame` and `reorderStoryboardFrames` — thin doors over
  the manager's two verbs, answering the manager's own boolean. A `false` (unknown frame, duplicate id,
  unknown board) is passed through, not swallowed; a removal leaves the survivors' `order` exactly as
  the manager kept it — a hole is honest state, and the panel does not renumber behind the reader's
  back. `StoryboardManagerLike` grows the two methods, so a fake that cannot edit fails here rather
  than in the browser.
- **Face** (`AssetPanel.tsx`): each frame row carries `↑` / `↓` / `remove` (edge buttons disabled —
  the first row cannot move up). Reorder swaps the two neighbours the button names and hands the
  manager the FULL id sequence, because resequencing is the manager's word. Neither verb touches the
  library — the frames reference assets, they are not assets, and the report's byte counts cannot move
  because there are none.
- **The measured defect the dispatch bar prevented, again**: the first fake's storyboards could not
  edit, which is exactly what `StoryboardManagerLike` growing the two methods now catches at typecheck.
  The unit block pins the manager's semantics as NUMBERS: after removing the middle of three, the
  orders read `[0, 2]` — the hole stays — and after a full reorder they read `[0, 1, 2]` again, in the
  sequence GIVEN.
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/assets.test.ts` **24 → 30 cases** (remove drops and leaves the hole; reorder
  rewrites; both refuse unknown/duplicate ids with the board untouched; neither verb moves the library
  or any byte); `tools/harness/studio-assets.mjs` — the REAL browser, **29/29 → 34/34**: every row
  carries its three controls with the edges disabled, move-down reorders (bridge order AND DOM row
  follow), remove drops the middle frame and the surviving orders read `[0, 2]` on the bridge, and the
  library still holds all four assets. apps/studio **332 → 338** (27 files), `tsc` and `eslint`
  (`--max-warnings=0`) clean.
- **Bounds (§60).** The surface can now edit the board's MEMBERSHIP and ORDER; it cannot yet rename a
  frame or change its duration (`updateFrame` has no product door), and there is no frame-ADD form —
  the board is still composed by the surface itself at mount. Character consistency and asset update
  still have no product surface. Nothing renders a board as pixels; there is no video, still.

## Amendment 189 — characters are ANCHORED and DERIVABLE: register and apply reach the consistency manager, apply answers a request and never an asset (M3 v189)

M3's open list is down to one. The consistency trio — `registerCharacter` / `listCharacters` /
`applyConsistency` — has lived in the package since before v160, and the AGENT lane has had its doors
since v160 (`asset.character.register` / `list` / `apply`); nothing in the Studio imported any of it.
v189 is the product face, and it keeps the lane's one rule: **APPLY ANSWERS A REQUEST, NEVER AN
ASSET** — no generator runs, because no generator is attached.

- **Pure layer** (`assets.ts`): `registerCharacter` and `applyCharacterConsistency` — thin doors over
  the manager's verbs. `CharacterManagerLike` is the structural seam (method syntax, so the real
  class's wider `applyConsistency` parameter satisfies it), and `DerivedRequestLike` asks only for the
  fields the summary reads. An unknown character is the MANAGER's own throw, quoted as it came —
  `no character registered as "nobody"` passes through untouched.
- **The measured crux is TWO numbers that must NOT agree.** The report says what the manager HOLDS: a
  strength nobody registered reads `null` — the same null-means-absent rule a still's `duration`
  follows. The derived summary says what the manager WOULD SEND: the manager's own `?? 0.8` default
  lands there. The unit fake and the headless proof both pin the pair — mira holds `null` at rest and
  her derivation carries `0.8` — because a surface that pre-applied the default into the report would
  be showing the reader a number the register does not own.
- **Face** (`AssetPanel.tsx`): a Characters section with a register form (id, an anchor select over
  the assets the library ACTUALLY holds, an optional strength) and one `apply prompt` button per row.
  The panel refuses what the manager would silently hold — an empty id, no anchor, a strength outside
  (0, 1] — and the derived line names itself: `no generator ran`.
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/assets.test.ts` **30 → 36 cases** (register holds null vs a given 0.5; apply
  carries the manager's 0.8 where none was held; the ask's type crosses untouched; the unknown
  character throws the manager's own words; register and apply move neither library nor generator);
  `docs/evidence/studio/asset-surface-proof.mjs` grew **§7** (the two numbers measured against the
  SHIPPED manager, assets unchanged) and the HEAD check became §8; `tools/harness/studio-assets.mjs`
  **34/34 → 41/41** — register mira/toma in the REAL browser, the rows read `none held` and `0.5`,
  mira's derivation shows the manager's `0.8` landing where the register held none, and the library is
  untouched. apps/studio **338 → 344** (27 files), `tsc` and `eslint` (`--max-warnings=0`) clean.
- **Bounds (§60).** A character is an anchor SET, not an asset: nothing stores bytes, nothing renders
  a picture, and the derived request is a SUMMARY the panel shows, not a payload it keeps. The
  surface cannot yet EDIT or DELETE a registered character (re-register is the manager's upsert), and
  there is no character UPDATE door. `asset.update` is the last open item on M3's list.

## Amendment 190 — the library is EDITABLE: updateMetadata's product door lands, and M3's open list is EMPTY (M3 v190)

- **The door.** The `asset.update` agent door has existed since v160, and its FIRST sentence is a
  refusal: *a patch that names nothing would be reported as an update by the library, so this door
  refuses it* — the library answers `true` for a patch that changes NOTHING, and a success that
  updated nothing is the class of defect this family exists to refuse. v190 is that door's product
  face, and it keeps the refusal. What may be patched is METADATA only: name, description, tags —
  an asset's BYTES and its id are not editable, and the form offers no way to try. The merge is over
  what the library HOLDS, so what the patch leaves out keeps its value, and the library's own
  `false` (an id it does not hold) is passed through and SHOWN, not swallowed.
- **Pure layer.** `AssetMetadataPatch` (name?/description?/tags?) — the same shape the door calls
  `AssetPatch` — plus one thin passthrough, `updateAssetMetadata(library, assetId, patch)`, answering
  the LIBRARY's boolean. `AssetLibraryLike` grows `updateMetadata`; `StudioAssetSummary` grows
  `description: string | null` (read verbatim from the metadata the library holds — `null` where none
  was given, the same null-means-absent rule a still's `duration` follows), because a row that
  cannot show the description would leave the patch half-invisible.
- **The refusal is the panel's.** The pure layer does not police the patch; the FORM does. Filled
  fields go into the patch verbatim (tags split on commas, blanks dropped), and a patch that names
  nothing is refused in the door's own words BEFORE any bytes could move. The UI is a two-state
  input: an empty field means "leave it alone", not "clear it" — the door's `''`-clears-tags reading
  is a three-state arg the form does not pretend to have.
- **Face.** The Library section gains an update form — asset select + three optional fields + an
  update button that is disabled until an asset is picked. The asset row now reads its tags back
  (`tags a, b` where tags exist), and the bridge report carries the description.
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/assets.test.ts` **36 → 41 cases** (a patch renames and the report reads the
  new name; the merge keeps what the patch leaves out; bytes and id are NOT editable — payload stays
  zero, id stays put; an unknown id is the library's own `false`; the count neither grows nor
  shrinks); `docs/evidence/studio/asset-surface-proof.mjs` grew **§9** (measured against the SHIPPED
  library: rename + description + tags land, `updatedAt` re-stamped, id and zero bytes untouched, an
  unknown id answered `false`, the report reads the merge back); `tools/harness/studio-assets.mjs`
  **41/41 → 46/46** — the form exists and is disabled until a pick, the empty patch is refused in the
  door's own words, the rename + tags land in the row, the bridge carries the description, count and
  zero bytes unchanged. apps/studio **344 → 349** (27 files), `tsc` and `eslint`
  (`--max-warnings=0`) clean.
- **Bounds (§60), and M3's list.** The patch is metadata-only BY DESIGN — an asset's bytes exist only
  as an empty payload in DEMO MODE, and no id ever moves. The panel refuses an empty patch but the
  pure layer does not (the door's refusal is the caller's discipline, and the harness asserts the
  panel keeps it). M3's open list is now EMPTY: the surface cannot PLAY footage, characters have no
  UPDATE/DELETE, and the generators remain DEMO MODE — those are bounds, not open items; the
  capability the doors cover (generate, remove, update, board-edit, characters) is all reachable
  from the product.



## Amendment 191 — the world REALLY persists: the engine's own save()/load() gain a disk lane, and the live world can be a saved one (M4 v191)

- **The lane.** M4's "Still open" has named disk persistence since v162, and the shape it takes is
  v184's: the browser holds the LIVE engine (`WorldPanel` composes it), the engine's own `save()`
  produces the file and its own `load()` consumes it, and `src/lib/worldSaveServer.ts` is only the
  disk between them. The store is the SAME tested one the scene lane rides — the runtime's
  `createFsSaveStore` over the REAL `node:fs` (reused from `saveFsServer`, so no second naming
  policy is invented next to it) — under a new root, `.nexus/world-saves`, the same gitignored
  `.nexus` the scene saves and the deploy records live in. The route (`app/api/agent/world-saves`)
  is the only door (GET probe + POST `write`/`read`), the browser holds a fetch adapter
  (`worldSaveLane.ts`) that imports nothing from `@nexus/three-runtime` or `node:fs`, and
  unavailability is a normal answer, not an error.
- **The one world-specific rule.** A file that does not carry an object `world` is not a world save.
  It is refused by name BEFORE any byte moves (write) or BEFORE it reaches the loader (read) — the
  engine's loader deserves a file it can actually parse, not a `TypeError` one seam away from the
  bytes that caused it. Everything else is the store's own words: a refused name, a missing file and
  non-JSON bytes all arrive as `ok: false` plus the store's sentence, paraphrased by nobody.
- **Face.** The world surface gains a Persist row — `save to disk` (engine.save() → parse → lane
  write → the note reports the byte count and the name), `browse disk` (probe → rows, click a row to
  load it), and a note that names the disk (`.nexus/world-saves`) rather than implying something
  vaguer. Loading hands the file back to the engine's own `load()` and re-reads the report: the live
  world BECOMES the saved one. The surface states the bound in its own footnote — the demo
  composition returns only when the surface remounts.
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/worldSaveServer.test.ts` (8 cases: lane facts as data, write → probe → read
  round trip, a refused name is the store's own sentence, a non-object and a worldless file are
  refused before any byte moves, read tells its four failures apart by name, a REAL-engine
  compose → save → write → read → load round trip is lossless, and a tmpdir round trip lands a REAL
  file) + `src/lib/worldSaveLane.test.ts` (7: probe passthrough, non-200 and unreachable are honest
  unavailability, the POST body shape, refusal and non-JSON bodies pass through). `tools/harness/
  studio-world.mjs` **25/25 → 34/34** — the persist row exists, the save note reports bytes, the
  file is read back off the REAL disk with node:fs AT THE TICK THE BRIDGE REPORTED (6), the rows
  list it, one step PAST the save (7) then load and the bridge counts the SAVED tick again (6) with
  the bonds restored from both sides. apps/studio **349 → 364** (30 files), `tsc` and `eslint`
  (`--max-warnings=0`) clean, `next build` clean with the route registered.
- **Bounds (§60).** `@nexus/world-engine` is UNTOUCHED — its lossless save/load, verified in v162,
  is the whole story; this amendment adds no engine code, only a disk for the file to rest on. The
  world panel has no delete/rename verbs yet (the scene panel's v186 verbs are the precedent), a
  load replaces the live world in place (the demo is the initial state, not a fresh sibling the way
  the 3D surface's demo scene is), and the engine's own `autoSaveInterval` stays 0 in the panel —
  persistence here is a verb the surface performs, not a timer it starts.

### Amendment 192 (M5 v192, studio) — the picked body gets an INSPECTOR, read from the LIVE scene at report time — and a body that has left the scene reports NOTHING rather than stale facts

_Numbering: 192 was free (`grep -ao "^### Amendment 1[0-9][0-9]"` topped out at 191). Full narrative in
`docs/evidence/studio/README.md`; this is the ledger entry._

- **The gap this closes.** v182 made a body PICKABLE: a click named it and the HUD printed the name. That is
  a label, not information — the panel could say WHICH body was picked and nothing about it. v192 adds the
  facts: kind, world position and visibility.
- **Read at REPORT time, not remembered from the pick.** `selectionFactsOf(scene, selected)` reads the live
  scene every time a report is built, and all seven of the surface's report call sites pass the current
  selection. A report that cached the facts at pick time would describe a body where it USED to be, which is
  the failure the proof exists to catch: it moves a body +3 through the runtime and asserts the reported x
  moves with it, with no re-pick.
- **The position is compared against the runtime's own object, not a constant.** The frame loop BOBS every
  body, so the live y is a fraction that changes per frame (measured: `0.0022` headlessly, `0.1269` in the
  browser). A proof asserting `-1.6, 0, 0` would pass against an inspector that invented its numbers; this
  one asserts agreement with `threeObject.position`, which the controller pins to `transform.position`.
- **A fact the report refuses to invent.** `position: SceneVec3 | null` — null when the host declares no
  position, the same rule as `duration: null` on the asset surface, one surface over. `kind` answers
  `'unknown'` for a host that declares no type rather than guessing one.
- **A body that LEAVES the scene has nothing to inspect.** The selection stays the NAME it was (the two are
  separate state) and the inspector answers `null`; nothing invents a position for a body that is gone. A
  pick that hits empty space clears the selection and with it the facts — no stale rows about a body nobody
  picked.
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/scene3dSurface.test.ts` gains the inspector cases over the REAL runtime;
  `scene-surface-proof.mjs` gains **§7** (renumbering HEAD to §8) and, with it, a **deterministic
  `pickAt` on the proof's adapter** — the real raycaster needs a GL context and a raycaster's accuracy is
  v182's subject, so this proof supplies the seam and exercises the surface's own `pickAt` path rather than
  reaching into it; `tools/harness/studio-scene3d.mjs` — the REAL browser, **53/53 → 55/55**: the probe picks
  Cube A, checks the report and the HUD carry `mesh` / a position / `visible`, then clears the selection and
  checks both answer nothing. apps/studio **332 → 369** (29 files), `tsc` clean.
- **A defect the section found in ITSELF.** The first draft set the pick target to null and then read the
  report WITHOUT performing the miss-pick, so it expected a clearing no call had performed — `actual:
  {id, name: 'Cube A'}, expected: null`. The pick is now made explicitly. A section that asserts a state
  change must perform the action that causes it.
- **Bounds (§60).** The inspector reports FOUR facts a host declares (id, name, kind, position, visibility).
  It does not read components, materials, children, animation state or anything else the runtime holds, and
  it cannot EDIT any of them — there is no setter, and the panel renders the facts as text.

### Amendment 193 (M7 v193, nexus-api + evidence) — HOSTED PUBLISH stops being deferred: a real Spring Boot service, a real PostgreSQL, and a publication that outlives the process that wrote it

_Numbering: 193 was free (`grep -ao "^### Amendment 1[0-9][0-9]"` topped out at 192). This is item 9 of the
priority queue in `docs/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`, and the first increment in this repository that needs a
backend at all. Full narrative in `docs/evidence/m7/README.md`; this is the ledger entry._

- **The bound this closes, which had been written down every time.** M1 deferred hosted publish to M7. Every
  milestone since ended with the same sentence — most recently the M6 deploy face's own record: *"deploy means
  RECORDS on this server — not a push, not a publish, not a release"*. v193 is the first thing here that runs
  a real service against a real database and reads back what it stored.
- **`services/nexus-api` is real, not a contract shell.** ADR 0011 fixed the stack (Java 25 + Spring Boot +
  PostgreSQL); this implements the first slice of it: **Spring Boot 3.5.16 on Java 25**, web + JPA + the
  Postgres driver, and nothing else — no Redis, no security, no AI-services boundary, because each starter
  added is a dependency the service owes an answer for later.
- **Two endpoints and one aggregate.** `POST /projects/{id}/publish` answers **201** with a receipt when the
  id was new and **200** when it already had a publication; `GET /projects/{id}` answers the publication or
  **404**. A RECEIPT does not echo the document back (the caller just sent it, and an echo grows with the
  payload); a READ does carry it (that is what reading a publication is for).
- **The URL is built from the request that asked** (`ServletUriComponentsBuilder`), so it names an address
  that actually serves the publication rather than a configured "public base" that could point at nothing.
  The bound is stated with it: **this is this server's URL** — no CDN, no rewrite, no custom domain.
- **Four rules, each with a reason.** A project id must be usable (a row keyed by a blank id is a row nothing
  can address); a title must be non-blank (a name the SERVER invented is not a fact about the project); the
  document must be a JSON **object** (not "valid JSON" — `42` parses and is not a design document), stored
  VERBATIM afterwards because this service is a record, not an interpreter; and re-publishing **updates** the
  row and increments its version, because "the publication of project X" must have exactly one answer.
- **Three defects the proof found that reading would not have.** (1) The receipt reported an instant with
  **nanosecond** precision while PostgreSQL stores **microseconds** — `…01.824829200Z` against a read-back of
  `…01.824829Z`, a receipt claiming precision the database had already dropped; the service now truncates to
  microseconds, and a unit case pins it. (2) `PublishRequest.document` was declared a `String`, so Jackson
  rejected every well-formed publish with a 400 — the contract is a JSON OBJECT, and the DTO now says so.
  (3) The proof itself read a process's exit as `exitCode !== null`, but **a process killed by a signal has
  `exitCode === null` and `signalCode` set** — so its restart waited forever for a service that had already
  died.
- **The proof runs the REAL thing, and says what it needs.** `docs/evidence/m7/publish-proof.mjs`: checks
  Java 25 and a reachable Docker daemon, builds the jar with Maven, starts a throwaway
  `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` on a port nothing else holds, starts the service on **port 0** and reads the port
  the service itself wrote, then asserts: 201 + a URL naming this server · the document deep-equal as JSON
  (which is what catches double-encoding) · re-publish → version 2 with the **DATABASE counted at exactly one
  row** · refusals answering 400 with their rule named and an unpublished id answering 404 · **the
  publication surviving a service RESTART** · and a teardown that removes the container even when an
  assertion failed.
- **Configuration crosses as ARGUMENTS, and the reason is measured.** The first version exported
  `NEXUS_API_PORT`; the service ignored it and bound a constant 61212 that this host's own tooling holds.
  `--debug` showed `--server.port=18099` taking effect while the same value in the environment did not, which
  is what an injected `SERVER_PORT` looks like — it outranks a `${…}` placeholder in `application.yml`.
  Command-line arguments outrank environment properties in Spring Boot, so they are what a proof must use: a
  proof should not be at the mercy of the ambient environment.
- **Evidence.** `services/nexus-api/src/test` — **14 cases**, no Spring context and no database, because
  "a blank title is refused" should not need one; `docs/evidence/m7/publish-proof.mjs` — the run above,
  against a real PostgreSQL 16 in Docker on a daemon reporting 29.8.2; `mvn -B test` BUILD SUCCESS.
- **Bounds (§60).** No auth, no accounts, no ownership — anyone who can reach it can publish any id. No
  listing (the repository has no finder beyond the inherited ones; listing is the NEXT slice). `ddl-auto:
  update` rather than migrations, because there is one table and one writer. A publication is REPLACED, not
  versioned: re-publishing bumps a counter and the previous document is gone. The document is stored, not
  understood — no validation beyond "is a JSON object". And **the Studio does not call this service yet**:
  v193 is the backend half, and the Publish control that reaches it is the next increment.

### Amendment 194 (M7 v194, studio + evidence) — the Studio CALLS the service: a Publish control over a fetch-only lane, proven end to end against a real database

_Numbering: 194 was free (`grep -ao "^### Amendment 1[0-9][0-9]"` topped out at 193). This closes the half
v193 left open — its own record said *"the Studio does not call this service yet"*. Full narrative in
`docs/evidence/m7/README.md`; this is the ledger entry._

- **The gap this closes, in v193's own words.** v193 made `services/nexus-api` work and left it with no
  consumer: a working backend nothing called. v194 adds the Publish control, so a Studio document reaches the
  service and becomes a row.
- **The same three-file split v172 and v184 established.** `src/lib/publishServer.ts` holds the service's
  address (`NEXUS_API_URL`, defaulting to the local service) and does the fetching — server-side only.
  `src/app/api/publish/route.ts` is the hop (`GET` = probe, `POST` = `publish` | `read`, Node runtime).
  `src/lib/publishLane.ts` is the CLIENT adapter and imports nothing from either, so the browser bundle never
  learns the service's address. The toolbar gains a Publish button and a note.
- **The Studio computes NOTHING it did not write.** It sends the project, the title and the document; the
  version, the instant and the URL come back from the service and are passed through unchanged. A Studio that
  computed a version or built a URL itself would be reporting its own guess about a record it did not write —
  and the proof checks the shown URL is the SERVICE's (`http://127.0.0.1:<service-port>/projects/…`), not one
  the Studio assembled.
- **"The service is not running" is a NORMAL answer.** The control probes on mount so it can say what it will
  do before it is pressed, and a down service is reported as `available: false` with a reason rather than as
  an error banner — `services/nexus-api` not running is the ordinary state of a frontend-first repository.
  A refused publish keeps the SERVICE's own sentence (`document must be a JSON object, got string`), because
  that sentence names the rule that was broken and "publish failed" does not.
- **The end-to-end proof stands up ALL THREE LAYERS.** `tools/harness/studio-publish.mjs` starts a throwaway
  PostgreSQL, builds and starts the real service on a port the OS picks, starts the REAL Studio dev server
  pointed at it, and drives the Publish button in a real browser — **11/11 assertions**: the toolbar reports
  the service ready · pressing Publish reports a publication · the id is parsed from the URL the SERVICE
  returned · the publication is read back **independently of the browser** · the shown URL is the service's ·
  a second press reports **version 2** with the **DATABASE counted at exactly one row** · the stored
  document's name and node count both match the Studio's · it is a JSON object · and teardown removes the
  container and both processes.
- **The proof starts the Studio ITSELF, and the order is part of the subject.** Every other harness probe
  requires a Studio on :3210. This one cannot: the service binds a port the OS picks and the Studio's route
  reads `NEXUS_API_URL` at request time, so a Studio started first would point at the wrong address.
- **One thing the proof deliberately does NOT claim.** It compares the stored document to the Studio's by
  NAME and NODE COUNT, not byte for byte: `window.__nexus.snapshot()` is a frozen read-only summary that
  carries neither the canonical document nor its id — which is also why the project id is taken from the
  service's URL. "The document matches" would be a claim about bytes this proof never saw, so it says which
  two facts it compared instead.
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/publishServer.test.ts` — 10 cases with an injected `fetch` (the receipt passes
  through unchanged, the project id is URL-encoded so a slash cannot change the path, the service's refusal
  sentence is kept, and a down service is a normal answer); `tools/harness/studio-publish.mjs` — the run
  above, with a PNG under `docs/evidence/m7/harness/`. apps/studio **369 → 379** (30 files), `tsc` clean.
- **Bounds (§60).** Publishing is a button in the toolbar, not a product surface: no project picker, no
  publish history, no unpublish, no "who published this", and no auth — the service takes any id from anyone
  who can reach it. The Studio does not READ a publication back in its UI (the lane can; nothing renders it),
  and a publication still REPLACES the previous one rather than versioning it.

### Amendment 195 (M7 v195, nexus-api + studio) — listing and unpublish: what is published, and taking one down — and a proof bug that hid behind a green check

_Numbering: 195 was free (`grep -ao "^### Amendment 1[0-9][0-9]"` topped out at 194). This is item 11 of the
priority queue in `docs/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`. Full narrative in `docs/evidence/m7/README.md`; this is the
ledger entry._

- **The gap this closes.** v193's own record listed it: *"No listing (the repository has no finder beyond the
  inherited ones; listing is the next slice)"* and *"No unpublish"*. A publishing feature that cannot say
  what is published and cannot take anything down is a one-way door.
- **The first finder on the repository, and it is a `Pageable` on purpose.** `findAllByOrderByPublishedAtDesc`
  reaches the DATABASE with the cap rather than reading everything and trimming in memory — which would work
  until the table is large and then be a table scan on every page load. Still no `findByTitle`: a search has
  its own rules (ranking, paging, a blank query) and an unproven surface is worse than a missing one.
- **The cap is CLAMPED, a non-positive limit is REFUSED, and the answer says which cap it used.** Asking for
  10 000 gets `MAX_LIST_LIMIT` (100) because "as many as you will give me" is a legitimate thing to mean and
  a 400 would make the caller guess the number; asking for 0 is a 400 because there is no honest reading of
  "fewer than one". The listing carries `count` AND `limit`, so a caller can tell "there are twenty" from
  "there are at least twenty" — a bare array cannot say that.
- **A listing entry carries NO document.** 100 entries must not mean 100 documents; the caller who cares
  about one gets it with the read endpoint it already has. The proof asserts the key is absent rather than
  merely empty.
- **Unpublish answers the store's own boolean.** `removed: true` when a row was deleted, `removed: false`
  when there was nothing to take down — 200 either way, because the URL names a PROJECT, not a resource that
  must exist. Taking down what is already down is a caller's mistake, not a corrupt store; the same rule the
  Studio's disk lane uses for a delete of a name that is not there.
- **The Studio's Publish face grew a list.** The lane gained `list` and `unpublish` (the route gained a
  `list` action, which is the one action that names NO project and is therefore answered before the
  `projectId` guard rather than being given a sentinel id to satisfy it). The toolbar's Published button
  opens a panel whose rows are the SERVICE's answer, re-fetched after every verb — never hand-edited, so a
  row that is gone cannot linger.
- **A PROOF BUG that had been hiding behind a green check.** `publish-proof.mjs` waited for postgres with
  `docker exec … pg_isready`, which runs INSIDE the container and therefore says nothing about the HOST port
  mapping — and it is the host mapping the service connects through. A `-p` that lost a race for the port
  passes the inside check and then leaves the service hanging on a datasource it can never reach, which reads
  as "the service is broken". The proof now ALSO polls a host-side TCP connection and fails with a sentence
  that names the difference. This is why the new sections could not be added until it was fixed: the failure
  appeared as a service that would not start.
- **Evidence.** `services/nexus-api/src/test` **14 → 21 cases** (the default cap reaches the repository as a
  `PageRequest` · a limit above the cap is clamped, asserted through an `ArgumentCaptor` · a non-positive
  limit is refused BEFORE the repository is asked · unpublish deletes when it exists and answers `false`
  without touching the repository when it does not); `src/lib/publishServer.test.ts` **10 → 17 cases** (the
  listing passes the limit through and reports the SERVICE's cap, an entry carries no document, a DELETE goes
  to the encoded project URL, "already down" is `ok: true` with `removed: false`); `publish-proof.mjs` gains
  **§6 listing and §7 unpublish** against the real database (newest-first checked against the instants, the
  cap reported, the row counted out of the DATABASE at 0); `tools/harness/studio-publish.mjs` **11 → 15/15**,
  driving the Published button and the take-down control in a real browser. apps/studio **379 → 386** (30
  files), `tsc` clean.
- **Bounds (§60).** No paging beyond the cap — a caller that wants the 5000th publication is asking a
  question this service does not answer yet. No ownership: anyone who can reach the service can unpublish
  anything. No soft delete and no history: a taken-down publication is gone, and there is no record that it
  existed. Listing returns metadata only, and the Studio's list shows at most 20 rows with no way to page.

### Amendment 196 (M7 v196, studio) — the ARTIFACT PAGE: a published project at a URL a person can open, drawn by the Studio's own renderer

_Numbering: 196 was free (`grep -ao "^### Amendment [0-9][0-9][0-9]"` topped out at 195). This is item 12 of
the priority queue in `docs/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md`, and it closes the thing **M1 explicitly deferred to M7**:
*"Hosted publish deferred to M7."* Full narrative in `docs/evidence/m7/README.md`; this is the ledger entry._

- **The gap this closes.** v193–v195 built the API half: a publication is a row, it can be read, listed and
  taken down. Every one of those is reachable only by a CLIENT that already knows the id. A person with a
  browser had nothing to open. `GET /p/{projectId}` is that missing half.
- **A route HANDLER, not a page, and that is the point.** What it answers with is not a React tree: it is the
  artifact, drawn by `renderPreviewHtml` — **the same function the Studio's local Preview and its HTML export
  use**. "What you published is what you get" is only true if the published page and the preview are the same
  code; a second renderer would be a second answer to the same question and the two would drift.
- **Three answers, and the status codes carry the difference.** `200` the artifact · `404` nothing is
  published under this id · `503` **the service** could not be reached or answered unusably. That last one is
  not a 404 on purpose: "nothing is published here" and "the thing that knows what is published is not
  running" are different facts, and a reader given the wrong one looks for the problem in the wrong place.
  The two failure PAGES say different things too, and a suite case asserts they are distinguishable.
- **A structural flag rather than a sentence match.** The route first decided 404-vs-503 by testing whether the
  lane's `reason` started with `"nothing is published"` — which would silently start answering 503 the day
  someone reworded that sentence. `readPublication` now reports `notFound: true`, and the route reads that.
- **A document that cannot be drawn gets its own page, not an empty stage.** A publication whose document is
  not an object, or whose `activePageId` names no page it holds, answers "Artifact unavailable" — because an
  empty stage looks like an artifact that happens to be blank rather than a broken record.
- **The panel links to it.** Each row of the Published panel gained an `open` link to `/p/{id}`. The link is
  one the STUDIO is the author of (it is the Studio's own route); the service's `url` names its JSON endpoint
  and stays what it is. Two addresses for two readers, and the code says so.
- **Two proof bugs found while adding this, both worth keeping.** (1) `studio-publish.mjs` had the SAME hole
  `publish-proof.mjs` had just been fixed for: it verified postgres with `docker exec … pg_isready`, which
  runs inside the container and says nothing about the host port the service connects through. Fixed the same
  way — a host-side TCP probe. (2) **The startup timeout sat at the median.** The service starts in ~12s on an
  idle machine and was MEASURED at **40.4s** while the machine ran containers and dev servers; both proofs
  waited 40s, so they failed intermittently for a reason unrelated to the code. The wait is now a named
  constant (180 tries × 1s) whose comment carries the measurement. **A proof whose timeout sits at the median
  is a proof that flakes.**
- **Evidence.** `src/lib/artifact.test.ts` — 5 cases (a publication renders the document through the
  renderer's own shell · a non-object document and a document naming no page both get the UNAVAILABLE page and
  NOT an empty stage · the missing and unavailable pages say different things and both escape caller-supplied
  text); `tools/harness/studio-publish.mjs` **15 → 20 assertions**, now drawing a rectangle first so the
  artifact has content, then fetching `/p/{id}` (200 + the stage), opening it in a REAL browser (the stage
  renders and has content), and checking an unpublished id answers 404 with its own page rather than the
  service-down page. apps/studio **386 → 391** (31 files), `tsc` clean.
- **Bounds (§60).** The artifact is the document and nothing else: no author, no publish date, no version, no
  navigation, no styling controls — a reader gets the drawing, not a page ABOUT the drawing. No auth: anyone
  who knows an id can open it, and anyone who can reach the Studio can publish or unpublish. The page renders
  the document with the preview renderer's fixed dark styling rather than the document's own `tokens` being
  themeable by the reader.

#### Amendment 196 — a landing note, written when the CODE finally landed

This record was written before its code, and the two landed in different commits. The paragraph above was
swept into `8ebdd75` (an M5 commit) by a `git add -A` that did not distinguish an in-flight M7 doc edit from
the M5 work being committed — so for a while the ledger described an artifact page the tree did not have.

Stated plainly, because the numbers above are deltas from when they were written and the tree has moved:

- **The count in the paragraph above (`386 → 391`, 31 files) was measured at the time of writing.** At
  LANDING, after the M5 line's v197–v203 had also landed, the same suite measures **391 → 407** in 31 files.
  Both numbers are true; they are true about different trees, and a reader deserves to know which.
- **The E2E probe is at `15 → 21/21`** — one assertion beyond the paragraph above: opening `/p/{id}` in a real
  browser and checking the stage renders WITH CONTENT (the probe now draws a rectangle before publishing, so
  the artifact is not an empty document that would pass a weaker check).
- The lesson is the one this ledger keeps relearning: **a doc edit in a dirty tree belongs to the commit that
  sweeps it, not to the increment it describes.** Commit the code and its record together, or the record will
  describe a tree that does not exist.

### Amendment 197 (M5 v197, studio) — the inspector's facts become EDITABLE, and the resolution plane a green suite could not see

_Numbering: 197 was free (`grep -ao "^### Amendment 19[7-9]"` matched nothing). The grant's own commit
(`d9976cb`) ends "ADR 0016 amendment 197 is OWED: the shared decisions file carries another lane's uncommitted
amendment draft; the record lands after that lane commits." This record pays that debt, written after the tree
had moved on — so its deltas are quoted as the readings taken on its landing day (2026-10-08), not as numbers a
later tree would answer._

- **The defect.** v192's inspector could READ a picked body's facts but not change them — its closing bound said
  "there is no setter and the HUD renders the facts as text". Two of the four declared facts become writable:
  the NAME and the VISIBILITY.

  picks — and `entity.threeObject.visible` in the renderer). The surface folds before the gate sees the ask
  (`clampEntityName` turns blank into a NO-ASK) and re-points the pick record ONLY on an ACCEPTED rename; the
  HUD gains rename and hide/show buttons whose labels state the ACTION while the data attribute states the
  STATE.

  **459/459**) while the REAL browser had neither gate: the first harness run failed at the hide-click check

  `@nexus/three-runtime` to `src/`, but the Studio's production build resolves the package's `main:
  ./dist/index.js` — and `dist/` was last compiled at v192, so the served bundle carried the surface's

  green. The unit seam proves the code; the harness proves the SHIPPED thing — and "shipped" means the compiled

  · harness 55 → **61/61** on next-start + headless Chrome (hide both records, reversible, a blank prompt counts

_Numbering: 198 was free. The grant's commit (`eea4f51`) says "ADR record owed behind v196/v197". This pays it._

### Amendment 199 (M5 v199, studio) — the inspector reads the component registry

_Numbering: 199 was free. The README section says the record is "OWED behind v196/v197/v198". This pays it._

- **The defect.** v197's inspector made the picked body's facts editable but still read only position and
  visibility — the runtime has a REAL component subsystem (`addComponent`/`removeComponent`/`getComponent` over
  a `Map` keyed by `component.type`, saved in the entry-array shape since v119) that the Studio never surfaced.
- **What landed.** The inspector reports each component's name and enabled state, and the HUD appends a
  `components:` segment ONLY when the registry is non-empty, naming a disabled component with an `(off)`
  suffix. The reader is a LOOSE one because the registry reaches the report through three spellings (the live
  `Map`, the entry array, a stringify object), all decoding to the same facts in their own order; `enabled !==
  false` follows the default-visible rule v192 set for bodies; a value with no readable `type` answers its key.
- **An honest negative recorded first.** Child counts stay uncounted: the runtime scene graph is FLAT (no
  entity parent/child API; children exist only on the renderer-level `threeObject.children`, which no runtime
  method exposes or counts). Inventing a `children` number from the renderer's internals would be exactly the
  fake-fact move this lane refuses.
- **Evidence.** Studio **404/404** (31 files; `scene3d` 72 → **74**, `scene3dSurface` 13 → **16** over the REAL
  runtime — `addComponent` answered in registry order, `removeComponent` followed) · three-runtime 463/463
  unchanged · harness 61 → **62/62** (the frozen read-only bridge cannot attach components, so the non-empty
  population is proven at the surface-suite and proof layers) · `scene-surface-proof.mjs` §7 drives both verbs
  through the shipped dist runtime. Measured 2026-10-08.

  proof layer drives the runtime's verbs directly); a component's `data` payload is not surfaced; materials,
  light state beyond v192's, and animation state remain unread.

### Amendment 200 (M5 v200, studio) — the component registry becomes EDITABLE

_Numbering: 200 was free. The v200 commit (`1eb6db7`) listed "ADR 0016 amendment 201" among its files but wrote
no record — and 201 is a DIFFERENT grant (v201's own). Neither 200 nor 201 was ever written. This record takes
200, the number its version names; 201 is written separately below._

- **The defect.** v199's inspector read the component registry but could not change it — `enabled` was a

- **What landed.** `setComponentEnabled(sceneId, entityId, componentType, enabled)` on the runtime, surfaced
  through the Studio as `toggleComponentEnabled(componentType)`, which flips the flag and re-reads the live
  registry for the report. It follows the host-gate pattern v197 set for rename/visibility: an optional method
  on the runtime the surface calls through; absent gate = unchanged report. The signature takes `(sceneId,
  entityId, ...)` like `setEntityName`/`setEntityVisible`. The runtime emits `'componentStateChanged'` when the
  flag changes (v200 does not invent a consumer). The HUD renders each component row as an interactive toggle
  button instead of text.
- **Evidence.** Studio **405/405** (31 files; `scene3dSurface` 16 → **17**) · three-runtime 463/463 unchanged ·
  harness **62/62** unchanged (the bridge is read-only, so the toggle is proven at the surface-suite and proof

  v192's, and child counts remain unread (v199's bounds hold); the `data` payload is not editable; there is no
