### Amendment 380 (M7/v387, services/nexus-api social) — the filed read's offset means ROWS, and the translation is pinned by tests

- **The gap, found while building the pager.** v382's filed door takes an `offset` → and the lane documents it as "the newest N of this account's reports →, STARTING AT offset" → — rows →. The service handed that number straight to `PageRequest.of(from, asked)` →, which reads its first argument as a PAGE INDEX →: a caller asking for the rows from 40 on was answered with the rows from 800 on →. With no test on the parameter → and no caller that paged yet →, the two meanings never met → — and the first pager to meet them would have jumped twenty windows per click → and called every page "past the end" →.
- **The fix.** The offset stays ROWS on the wire → (the name and the lane's words were the honest ones →); the service translates rows into the pages Spring Data speaks →: `PageRequest.of(from / asked, asked)` →. An offset that is not a whole window lands on the page boundary at or before it → — the only granularity a window has →, and the window whose rows the caller asked about →.
- **Files:** `services/nexus-api/src/main/java/dev/nexus/api/social/ReportService.java` (the translation →, with the reason in the comment →), `services/nexus-api/src/test/java/dev/nexus/api/social/ReportServiceTest.java` (+3 →: offset 40 with a window of 20 lands on page 2 — rows 40–59 →, not 800–819 →; offset 25 lands on the boundary at or before it →; a negative offset is the first window →).
- **Measured (2026-10-23):** `mvn -B test -o` → **249 tests, 10 classes, 0 failures, 0 errors, BUILD SUCCESS** (+3 →); `apps/studio` **1282/1282 (67 files)** → and `npx tsc -p apps/studio/tsconfig.json` → **exit 0** → — no client change was needed →, because the pager (v386) had already been written in the semantics the wire promised →.
- **Bounds (§60).** The translation is page-granular →: an offset of 25 answers rows 20–39 →, not 25–44 →. A pager that moves by whole windows never notices →; a caller asking for an arbitrary row offset gets the window containing it →, which is stated here rather than discovered later →.

### Amendment 381 (M9/v388, services/nexus-api ops + apps/studio + evidence) — the trail's window can be PAGED, in rows, with two different honest endings

A creator tipped thirty-seven times was told there were thirty-seven →, shown twenty →, and had no way to reach the other seventeen →; a reader who gave thirty-seven could read only the twenty they gave most recently →.

The two sides page INDEPENDENTLY →: the received set and the given set are two different questions about two different sets →, and one page for both would answer neither →. The lane echoes the window it asked for →, so two reads in flight cannot be mistaken for each other's answers →; the Studio's own door forwards the offset with a negative clamped to the first window →. - **And the window line says which rows, past the first.** "the N newest of M" on the first window →, "showing 21–40 of 37" past it → — v386's correction →, the fourth and fifth lists to receive it →. An empty window on a LATER page says "this page is past the end" →, not "nobody has given this account anything" → — a fact about one window must not be told as a fact about the whole list →.

### Amendment 386 (v393, packages/ai-providers) — the router's honesty contract gets its tests: a refusal is BY NAME, and the badge tells the truth

- **The gap.** `ai-providers.test.ts` covered the router's happy demo paths →; what nothing pinned was the router's HONESTY contract → — the part a demo-mode product can most easily get wrong →. A provider that cannot serve →, a badge that claims one mode while another is in play →, an injected provider that is quietly ignored →: none of those fail loudly in demo mode →, which is exactly why they need a test that says so →.
- **A refusal is BY NAME, and it happens BEFORE the call.** Every task the router fronts gates on `available` →: an unavailable design provider refuses `design.generate` and `design.edit` with `ProviderUnavailableError` naming the task and the provider →, and the embedding →, rerank and image tasks get the same gate →. The provider's method is never invoked → — a dead key can never look like an empty answer →.
- **And a refusal records NOTHING.** The cost engine reads the recorder →; a refused call that still recorded usage would bill a reader for an answer they never got →, so the recorder's call count stays at zero →.
- **The badge tells the truth.** `mode` reports `'live'` the moment a live provider is injected → — the UI cannot claim demo while a live capability is in play → — and a DEMO provider that cannot serve still reports `'demo'` →: the badge is about which capability is in play →, not about whether it is up right now →.
- **And an injected provider is the one that serves.** The custom design provider's `generate` and `edit` are each called once →, the router returns their result →, and their usage lands in the recorder the router was built with → — a router that ignored its injections would pass every demo-mode test while serving nobody's live key →.
- **Files:** `packages/ai-providers/test/router.test.ts` (+8 cases →, the only file →).
- **Measured (2026-10-23):** `npx vitest run` in `packages/ai-providers` → **66/66 (8 files)** (+8 →), BUILD green →. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports one error that exists on HEAD without this change →: `call-recorder.test.ts` imports `type Usage` from `call-recorder.js` →, which does not export it → — named here rather than quietly assumed →, and left alone as out of scope for a test-only increment →.
- **Bounds (§60).** The fakes are hand-written providers implementing the four interfaces →; no network and no live key is exercised →, by construction →. The `mode` getter considers the design →, embedding and image ids and NOT the reranker's → — a live reranker alone leaves the badge at `'demo'` →, which reads as deliberate (the badge is about the design capability →) but is unpinned either way →, named here rather than assumed →.

### Amendment 387 (v394, packages/ai-providers) — the call-recorder test imports Usage from the module that declares it, and the package typecheck is green again

- **The gap.** `call-recorder.test.ts` imported `type Usage` from `call-recorder.js` →, which imports the type from `types.js` without re-exporting it → — so `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` answered **exit 2 on HEAD** before this change →. Vitest never noticed →: esbuild strips types without checking them →, so the suite was green while the package's own typecheck was red → — a gate that looks like it passes because nobody runs it is worse than no gate →.
- **The repair.** The import names the module that DECLARES the type → (`../src/types.js` →), which is where every other file in the package reads it from →. One import line →, no behavior change →, and the test count is unchanged →.
- **Files:** `packages/ai-providers/test/call-recorder.test.ts` (the import line →, the only file →).
- **Measured (2026-10-23):** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` in `packages/ai-providers` → **exit 0** (was exit 2 on HEAD →); `npx vitest run` → **66/66 (8 files)** →, unchanged →. `packages/world-engine`'s own typecheck → **exit 0** →, checked in the same pass so the repair is shown to be local →.
- **Bounds (§60).** The alternative repair — re-exporting `Usage` from `call-recorder.ts` → — would also have compiled →, and was rejected because the type is declared in `types.ts` and every other reader imports it from there →; a second export path for one type is a second place for the two to drift →.

### Amendment 388 (v395, apps/studio) — the profile page's tip bar PAGES, and its pager is a LINK because the page cannot act

- **The gap.** v350 gave the profile page's tip bar its window line ("showing the N newest of M") and v355 put the whole-table count on every answer, but the bar still read only the first TIP_LIMIT rows: a creator given 150 tips had 100 of them on the page, was told there were 150, and could not reach the other 50 →. The service's /tips door has paged by rows since v391 and the client lane has echoed the window it answered all along → — the page itself was the only side that could not move.
- **The repair.** TipBarFacts gains offset (which window, in the service's own rows), limit (the window's size, as the service answered it) and pageHref (how to build another window's URL) →. The window line is now position-aware: the first window says "the 100 newest of 101", a later one says "showing 101–150 of 150" (v386's correction), and an empty window past the end says "this page is past the end — the service answered an empty window" rather than reading as an account nobody ever tipped →. The pager is drawn as LINKS — the page is server-rendered and holds no session (ADR 0018), so the route is the layer that knows the URL and the bar draws an <a>; at a boundary the control is a <span> with no href, because a link that went nowhere would be a lie with an href →. "Older" is offered only when the NEXT window would hold something: the whole-table count rides on every answer, so a page the service has already counted as empty is a page the bar does not offer →. A bar given no pageHref draws no pager at all — a link it cannot build is a link it does not draw →. The route reads tipOffset (separate from the gallery's offset, so the two windows page independently) and keeps the reader's q and gallery page in the links it builds →.
- **Files:** apps/studio/src/lib/tipBar.ts (the three fields, the position-aware window line, the pager, the styles), apps/studio/src/app/u/[accountId]/route.ts (the tipOffset parameter, the URL builder, the offset and limit on the answer), apps/studio/src/lib/tipBar.test.ts (+7), tools/harness/studio-publish.mjs (§80 grades the first window, the second window and a window past the end, as HTML).
- **Measured (2026-10-23):** apps/studio **1304/1304 (67 files)** (+7); tsc -p apps/studio/tsconfig.json exit 0; the audit, trail and social contract proofs all exit 0 → — the tip answers gained fields on the client side only, and the proofs still read both sides as agreeing.
- **Bounds (§60).** The real-browser E2E could not run here (no Docker, no Java service); §80 drives the same fetch-the-page shape the profile checks have used since v270 and is graded on the next machine that can →. The pager is LINK-based by necessity, not by choice: a server-rendered page cannot flip a window without a round trip, and pretending otherwise would be a button that does nothing →. And this is the profile page's TIP bar — the plan bar and the follow bar on the same page still read through their own lanes and are unpaged, named here rather than quietly assumed →.

### Amendment 391 (v398, apps/studio) — every pager in the Studio ends on the NEXT window, not on this one

- **The gap.** v391 and v392 gave the pagers two different honest endings, and v395, v396 and v397 each replaced the weaker one on the side they were touching →. The tempting rule (v392) disables "Older" when the window ALREADY holds every row the service counted; the better rule (v391 onward) offers "Older" only when the NEXT window would hold something →. The two agree on every FULL window → they disagree exactly when the service answered with fewer rows than the cap while the count says more rows sit past the next window's start, and there the tempting rule sends the reader to a page the service has already counted as empty →. Nine pagers in the Toolbar were still on the tempting rule →.
- **The repair.** ONE rule, in one place: `olderWindowWouldHoldSomething(offset, windowSize, count)` in apps/studio/src/lib/pager.ts →. Rows exist at offsets 0..count-1, so "the next window would hold something" and "there is a row at offset + windowSize" are the same sentence, and the rule can never hide a reachable row →. A count that could not be read offers nothing rather than guessing (v288's rule: an unread count is not a count of nothing), and a window with no size names no page →. The nine pagers → the trail (unfiltered), the tips received, the tips given, the subscriptions held, the subscriptions received, the plans, the desk, the filed reports and the following list → all read the same helper now, so the ending is one sentence instead of nine →.
- **Files:** apps/studio/src/lib/pager.ts (new — the one rule, with the two-rules-disagree case written out), apps/studio/src/lib/pager.test.ts (new, +7), apps/studio/src/components/Toolbar.tsx (the nine disabled conditions, and the six comments that described the old ending).
- **Measured (2026-10-23):** apps/studio **1342/1342 (69 files)** (+7); tsc -p apps/studio/tsconfig.json exit 0; the audit, trail and social contract proofs all exit 0 → — a change to when a button is disabled, graded by the suite that already reads every panel's window lines.
- **Bounds (§60).** The trail keeps its heuristic on the FILTERED branch and the desk keeps its on the no-tally branch, because neither has a count of the set it is paging: the service's audit count is the WHOLE trail's, narrowed or not (v385), so a window that came back short of the cap remains the only honest ending available there → — named rather than quietly assumed. The rule is about the COUNT's word, so it inherits whatever the count is worth: a count read a moment before the rows can disagree with them, and the pager then offers a page that has since emptied → — the same race every windowed list here carries, and not one a pager can close.


### Amendment 392 (v399, apps/studio + services/nexus-api) — the artifact page’s comment thread PAGES, in rows, past the cap

- **The gap.** v286 made the artifact page’s comment thread a WINDOW (the service caps at a hundred comments) and v354 gave it a visible count, but the thread could never be PAGED: a reader on a thread longer than the cap saw its head, was told how many comments the thread held, and could not reach the older ones →. Every other windowed list learned to page long ago — the filed read (v382), the following list (v390), the plans (v392), the profile page’s tip, plan and follow bars (v395/v396/v397) — and the thread was the last big window on a public page that could not move.
- **The repair.** The same shape every other windowed read got, applied to the one door that was still missing it →. The offset is ROWS past the newest comments; Spring Data’s PageRequest speaks PAGES (v387’s lesson), so the translation is by whole windows →. A negative offset is the first window rather than a refusal — the newest comments are the honest answer to a question about a page before the first →. The answer carries the thread’s ROW count (the removed ones included), because the window pages by ROWS and the visible count is not a row count: a thread of fifty comments of which thirty were taken back has thirty visible and fifty rows, and a pager that used the visible number as its end would stop a reader twenty rows short of it →. The answer is a SEPARATE record (ThreadAnswer) from the author direction’s (CommentAnswer), because the author direction does not page and has no whole-table count — putting a window’s fields on its answer would name a window that was never asked for →. On the page, the window line is position-aware ("the 100 newest" on the first window, "showing rows 101–101 of 101" past it, v386’s correction), an empty window on a LATER page says "this page is past the end — the service answered an empty window" rather than reading as a publication nobody ever commented on, and the pager is LINKS the route builds — the page is server-rendered and holds no session (ADR 0018), so a link it cannot build is a link it does not draw →. "Older" is offered only when the NEXT window would hold something (v398’s one rule, shared now with every other pager in the Studio).

- **The gap.** v350 gave the like bar its window line and v336 named the likers, but the bar still read only the first window the service’s default allowed: a publication liked by more accounts than the cap had its older likers on the page as a COUNT and nothing else — the reader was told there were more and given no way to see them →. - **The repair.** The same shape the comment thread got, one door over →. The offset is ROWS past the newest likes; PageRequest speaks PAGES (v387’s lesson), so the translation is by whole windows →. A negative offset is the first window rather than a refusal →. The count needs no second number: a like is never soft-deleted — an un-like DELETES its row — so the whole count the bar has always carried IS the row count a pager pages by, unlike the comment thread’s answer (v399), which had to carry a separate total because removed comments keep their rows →. The list’s answer is a SEPARATE record (LikesAnswer) from the writes’ (LikeAnswer), because a like or an un-like is not a window: putting the window’s fields on their answer would name a window that was never asked for →. On the page, the window line is position-aware ("the 20 newest of 21" on the first window, "showing rows 21–21 of 21" past it, v386’s correction), an empty window on a LATER page says "this page is past the end — the service answered an empty window" rather than reading as a publication nobody liked, and the pager is LINKS the route builds — the page is server-rendered and holds no session (ADR 0018) →. "Older" is offered only when the NEXT window would hold something (v398’s one rule). The page’s window stays twenty — the service’s default — so the change adds a door and moves nothing that was already reachable.

### Amendment 394 (v401, packages/world-engine) — the CHARACTER AGENT’s own rules, graded directly rather than through the tick

- **The gap.** `CharacterAgent` has existed since v144 and has been exercised only THROUGH the engine’s tick: a simulation where the agent decided something, and an assertion about the world afterwards. That is coverage of the ENGINE and none of the agent — which actions it offers, which one it picks and why, and what an execution writes were never asked directly, and the two v162 repairs (a locationless character crashed `decide()`; a co-located character who was not a declared NPC could not be spoken to) were fixed without a case that names either rule →. A behaviour with no direct case is a behaviour the next refactor is free to break quietly.
- **The repair.** One file that asks the agent directly, in the agent’s own words →. The actions: `rest` is available to a character BETWEEN PLACES (the v162 crash, named as a case), a connected location offers a move priced by the connection’s distance, anyone CO-LOCATED can be spoken to, a declared NPC who is also an inhabitant is ONE candidate rather than two, an item on the ground offers a take, a hurt character is offered healing and a whole one is not, an ACTIVE goal offers a pursuit and a finished one does not →. The decision: the chosen action is among the available ones, the alternatives are other actions and at most three, the confidence sits in [0,1], a hurt or exhausted character RESTS rather than takes the road, and a character with nothing at all still gets `rest` rather than a crash or an invented action →. The execution: rest restores and caps, a move changes the location and writes an event naming both ends, a conversation writes a TWO-SIDED bond (first meeting at the floor, the second one grown on both sides), a DECLARED bond keeps its name while its number grows, a take moves the item from the ground into the inventory, and an action that is not available is REFUSED by name with no events →. And what the world can tell the agent: a fact is knowable, goal progress is clamped and a finished goal is COMPLETED, and somebody else’s goal is left alone.
- **Files:** packages/world-engine/test/characterAgent.test.ts (new, 25 cases).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** packages/world-engine vitest **75/75 (3 files)** (+25); `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 0 — the agent’s rules graded directly, and the engine’s own suite unchanged and still green.
- **Bounds (§60).** These are the agent’s OWN rules — the engine’s tick, the RAG retrieval and the persistence round-trip stay where they were graded (worldEngine.test.ts, worldRag.test.ts) →. The engine writes its own events into the timeline (a character was created, a location was created), so the recent-events case grades the rule on the events the test added — the character’s own and the public one, newest first, and somebody else’s secret not at all — rather than on the whole timeline →. And the scores themselves are not pinned: the case grades that survival OUTRANKS the road, not the exact number the weights produce, because a weight is a tuning and a tuning is allowed to move.

### Amendment 395 (v402, packages/world-engine) — the RELATIONSHIP core’s own rules, graded directly rather than through the tick

- **The gap.** v162 wrote the relationship arithmetic as pure functions and the engine’s tick has carried them ever since: a bond sat in a world, the world stepped, an assertion read the bond afterwards. That is coverage of the ENGINE and thin coverage of the RULES — the band edges were probed at six numbers in one case, the custom `perTick`/`floor`/`gain`/`cap` parameters never, and the claims the module’s own doc-comment makes (“decay never manufactures hatred”, “a declared bond is never retyped”, “absence wears a bond back to met-once”) were prose rather than cases. The same shape v401 found in the agent: a rule with no direct case is a rule the next refactor is free to break quietly.
- **The repair.** One file that asks the arithmetic directly, in its own words →. The constants are pinned — floor 10, cap 100, gain 5, decay 2, and the roster is EXACTLY the four derivable types in band order — and the floor is measured to BE the enemy/neutral edge while the cap sits inside the ally band →. The bands are swept, not spot-checked: every edge in its band, everything below the floor an enemy however far below, everything past the cap an ally, and a full sweep from −20 to 120 that never moves backward →. Decay takes the step and the floor it is given, converges from the cap to the floor in exactly 45 steps and then stops moving, and no strength in [0, cap] decays into the enemy band — the doc-comment’s “never manufactures hatred”, as a loop rather than a sentence →. Gain pays the declared step, caps at 100 from below and from above, and its one asymmetry is pinned honestly: a gain has NO floor, because the floor is written at first meeting by the agent, not enforced here →. And the two halves are composed: a bond tended every tick walks neutral → friend → ally on the arithmetic alone (friend at tick 10, ally at tick 15, capped at 18), and a bond neglected every tick walks ally → friend → neutral and rests at the floor.
- **Files:** packages/world-engine/test/relationships.test.ts (new, 20 cases).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** packages/world-engine vitest **95/95 (4 files)** (+20); `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 0 — the arithmetic graded directly, and the engine’s own suite unchanged and still green.
- **Bounds (§60).** These are the pure functions’ OWN rules — where the engine APPLIES them (the tick’s decay pass, a declared bond keeping its name) stays where it was graded (worldEngine.test.ts) →. The composed walks grade the arithmetic, not the engine’s choice to decay every unmaintained bond every tick — that policy is the engine’s, and it is tested there →. And the constants are pinned because the rest of the engine QUOTES them (the agent seeds a first meeting at the floor); a future tuning that moves a number will redden this file on purpose, which is the point of pinning it.

### Amendment 396 (v403, apps/studio) — the STUDIO STORE’s own authoring rules, graded directly rather than through a browser

- **The gap.** The zustand store has shipped since v132 and has never had a test file of its own: component/instance authoring (ADR 0015), the remix fork (v233) and the lineage stamp (v267) were graded only through the browser harnesses, which need a dev server and a real browser. The actions themselves are plain functions over a plain document — `get()`, a batch of ops, `set()` — so every rule in them was reachable headlessly and none of them was asked. A rule with no case is a rule the next refactor is free to break quietly — the third shape of the same gap v401 and v402 found in the world-engine.
- **The repair.** One file that drives the store directly →. `createComponent`: the selected layers move under a new master at the selection’s bounds, re-based onto the master’s origin, and an instance stands where they stood — and an empty selection, a locked layer and a layer that is not on the active page are all refused with the same sentence and no change →. `insertInstance`: a new instance at the staggered spot, sized from the master; an unknown component is refused by name →. `detachInstance`: the instance is replaced by concrete copies — no `componentId`, no overrides, the text keeps its letters — at the instance’s own layout position, and a selection with no instance is refused →. `setInstanceOverride`: the patch lands on the named master child and only there, in one op; width clamps at 1 and radius at 0 (a square corner is a value, not an absence); an empty patch on an already-empty override removes the key while an empty patch on a real override leaves it; a node that is not an instance is refused in silence →. `remixDocument`: the fork gets a FRESH id so publishing it can never overwrite the source, the `_lineage` stamp is written for the pages to read back, and the history starts empty — the source’s undo log is not inherited →. And `instanceView` keeps its memoization contract: the same document object answers with the identical projection, a different document recomputes, and the projection names the instance itself as well as its clones.
- **Files:** apps/studio/src/lib/store.test.ts (new, 17 cases).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** apps/studio vitest **1389/1389 (72 files)** (+17); `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 — the store’s authoring rules graded directly, and the whole studio suite still green.
- **Bounds (§60).** These are the STORE’s own rules — the canvas, the panels and the real-browser harnesses stay where they were graded (golden-path, world, assets) →. `generate`/`editSelection` are deliberately not graded here: they go through the DEMO-MODE router and are the composer’s subject, not the store’s →. And the suite is a singleton store: each case reloads a fresh document, so the cases share the module’s history only through `loadDocument`, which is itself one of the graded rules →. The browser-only surfaces (drag, on-canvas text edit, the 3D and World panes) remain harness work, unchanged by this file.

### Amendment 401 (v408, apps/studio) — the INTENT readers’ own rule, graded directly

- **The gap.** Nine pure readers — the comment, like, follow, subscribe, report and tip verbs and their four un-verbs — decide what the Studio DOES when a public page links a reader into it, and not one of them had a case. Each is a one-liner, which is exactly why they drifted ungraded: the rule is small enough to state exactly and small enough to break quietly. A reader that answered an empty id, or one verb’s parameter answering another verb’s question, would have opened a composer over nothing.

The id is read from ONE named key, with or without the leading question mark, and from among other parameters →. An absent, empty or whitespace-only value is NO intent rather than an empty id — the blank check trims →. And the edge the readers actually carry, pinned rather than smoothed: the check trims but the ANSWER does not, so a padded id is returned as it stands — the reader’s job is to say what the URL named, not to repair it, and a future trim is now a decision →. An encoded id is decoded, the FIRST value wins when a key repeats, and no reader answers for another verb’s parameter — the un-verbs read their own keys, not the base verb’s →.

### Amendment 402 (v409, apps/studio) — the GALLERY builder’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The gallery is shared by the explore page and the profile page, and it exists so the per-row fan-out (a second read for the document, a thumbnail drawn from it) is written ONCE rather than twice and drifting — and neither of its two functions had a case. `firstPageId` is the defensive read that decides whether there is anything to draw at all, and `buildGalleryItems` keeps the rule the module’s own doc-comment states: a row whose document cannot be read is shown WITH ITS REASON, never as a blank card.
- **The repair.** One file that drives both →. `firstPageId` answers null for anything that is not a document at all, for a missing or non-string active page id, for a document with no nodes map, and for a STALE active page id that names no node — the last one matters because a stale id is not a page, and drawing against it would be a lie about the document →. `buildGalleryItems`: each row is read once, in order, by its project id; a document with a live page is drawn and the card carries no note; a read that failed shows the read’s OWN reason, and a read with no reason still says “preview unavailable” rather than nothing; a document with no drawable page (or none at all) says “nothing to draw” — the card’s own fact, not a failure — and the drawer is never called for it; an empty listing reads nothing at all →. And the card keeps the row’s facts and the lineage the document carries, so the shared builder hands the renderer exactly what the two pages need.

### Amendment 403 (v410, apps/studio) — the PREVIEW renderer’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The artifact page and the gallery card both render a published document through `renderPreviewHtml`, and every value it writes comes from JSON a client posted — a publication is stored verbatim (v294 read a malformed style back out of the store to prove it). The renderer’s own comment names the nine document-derived fields that could end an attribute or close the style block, and the artifact tests exercise the renderer THROUGH the page — so the escaping itself, the module’s whole reason for the composed-attribute rule, was nobody’s direct subject.
- **The repair.** One file that drives the renderer directly →. Text characters are HTML-escaped — a publication cannot write markup through its words →. A token value carrying a quote cannot end the style attribute: the composed attribute is escaped WHOLE, so a field added later cannot be forgotten →. The `:root` block is CSS-escaped rather than HTML-escaped — CSS does not decode entities, so `<` travels as `\3c ` and the value survives as one character while the block stays closed →. And a token NAME is escaped like its value: a key of `x}</style><img src=y>` cannot reach the block as a rule →. The shape rules too: the stage is the page’s size from the layout, a rect is an absolutely positioned box at its layout rect, an ellipse is a 50% radius, a turned node carries its rotation, a text node carries the full shorthand, an image is the honest placeholder, an invisible node is not drawn, an unknown page id is an empty stage rather than a crash — and an instance’s bodies are PROJECTED, the clone drawn and not just the instance box, which is the line whose absence once made the artifact draw one div where the canvas drew two.
- **Files:** apps/studio/src/lib/preview.test.ts (new, 13 cases).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** apps/studio vitest **1539/1539 (79 files)** (+13); `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 — the renderer graded directly, and the whole studio suite still green.
- **Bounds (§60).** These are the RENDERER’s rules — the artifact page’s own chrome (byline, remix link, the two failure pages) stays where it is graded (artifact.test.ts), and the clip-path divergence for a turned child inside a turned frame is pinned there and in the module’s comment, not re-pinned here →. The token VALUES are escaped as written; what a well-formed token looks like is the editor’s subject, not the renderer’s →. And the escape is inert for every drawing the canvas itself could make — a well-formed CSS value holds none of `& < > " '\` — which is why the tests use deliberately hostile values.

### Amendment 404 (v411, apps/studio) — the PAINT resolver’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** `paint.ts` is the seam every renderer shares: the canvas puts its answers on a context, the artifact writes them into a `style` attribute, the thumbnail into SVG attributes. Its own comment names the reason the coercion lives here — a value that is really `'bold" onload="x'` would take three shapes of damage from one malformed style — and not one of those defenses had a case. A published document is JSON a client posted, so the malformed inputs are not hypothetical; they are the population.
- **The repair.** One file that asks the resolver directly →. The four paint kinds each answer in their own shape: a solid and a stroke are their rgba rounded to 8-bit channels, a token ref resolves through the document’s own tokens (a hex string passes through, an RGBA object is normalized), a linear gradient lists its stops in order with positions rounded to whole percents, and an image fill is the labeled placeholder rather than a broken url →. A token the document does not have is a NAMED grey — not transparent, not a crash — and `tokenColorCss` answers its fallback (the default and a caller’s own) for the same absence →. And the malformed-style defenses, which are the point of the module: a reference that is not a path resolves to nothing (family falls back to `Inter, sans-serif`, size to 16), a number that is not finite falls back rather than reaching a renderer as NaN, and an align that is not one of the three the model owns reads as `left` — one malformed style cannot take the gallery page down, and now that is graded rather than asserted in a comment.

### Amendment 405 (v412, apps/studio) — the shared ESCAPER’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** `escapeHtml` in `pageShell.ts` is the ONE escaper every server-rendered Studio page shares — drawn out of artifact.ts at v241 precisely because two copies of the rule would be two answers to “is this safe”. Every value it writes comes from JSON a client posted, and the module’s own comment names the ORDER as the load-bearing property: the ampersand runs first, so the entities the later rules introduce are never re-escaped. The pages were graded through their own tests, but the shared rule underneath them had no direct subject.
- **The repair.** One file that asks the escaper directly →. The five characters that can end an attribute or a text node each answer their own entity. The ORDER is pinned: `&` runs first, so `<b>` answers `&lt;b&gt;` and not `&amp;lt;` — an escaper that double-escapes is not safer, it is a different answer to the same question →. An already-escaped string is escaped AGAIN: the contract is one escape of raw text, so a double-write does not silently decode back into markup →. An attribute-breaking payload — `" onmouseover="alert(1)` — cannot break out; no quote survives in the answer →. And ordinary text — letters, digits, punctuation that is not one of the five, the empty string — travels untouched →.

### Amendment 406 (v413, apps/studio) — the CLAIM builder’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** `claimOf` is the ONE builder of the claim every social verb travels with — the like, comment, follow, tip, report and subscribe composers all call it, because a claim six modules build slightly differently is six shapes disagreeing about the same account (v288). A device with no account has NO claim — null, empty and whitespace-only ids all answer null, because an invented account id is an action nobody took →. Only the ID gates the claim: an account with neither handle nor assurance still carries one →. The id, handle and assurance each travel TRIMMED, and a blank handle or assurance answers null rather than an empty string — an absent field says so by name →. And `claimedAt` is ALWAYS null on this side: the interface allows a number so the SERVICE can carry one, but the browser’s builder never stamps a time, so a claim says when the service saw the act rather than when the browser decided to make it →.

### Amendment 407 (v414, apps/studio) — the SLUG namer’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** Three exports share one namer — `exportJson`, `exportHtml` and `exportCanvasPng` all end in `${slug(name)}-…` — and the slug itself had no case. The rule is three rewrites deep (lowercase, every run of non-alphanumerics to one hyphen, no leading or trailing hyphen), and its interesting edges are what it does NOT do: it does not rescue a name that reduces to nothing, and it does not transliterate. A download’s filename is the first part of an export a person sees, and it was graded by nobody.
- **The repair.** One file that asks the namer directly →. An empty name answers the fallback `nexus` — a document nobody named still downloads — and the check is falsiness, not emptiness, so any falsy answers the same →. A spaced name lowercases; a RUN of non-alphanumerics collapses to ONE hyphen rather than many; leading and trailing separators are stripped; digits and the fallback itself survive the rule unchanged →. And the honest edge, pinned rather than smoothed: a name with no ASCII alphanumerics — `你好`, `---`, a lone space — is truthy, so the fallback never fires and the rewrites leave the EMPTY string. The download is then `-snapshot.json`, and that is now a stated fact rather than a surprise →. The rule is also idempotent — slugging a slug changes nothing →.

### Amendment 409 (v416, apps/studio) — the storage I/O seam’s own contracts, graded directly

- **The gap.** `persist.ts` is pure and window-free by design, which makes `storage.ts` the ONLY module in the Studio that touches `window` (ADR 0002 testability) — and the seam itself had no case. Its contracts are small and load-bearing: the two fakes must answer the KvStore shape exactly (a missing key is null, an empty string is a VALUE), the browser resolution must DEGRADE rather than dereference, and the one key every saved document lives under is a fact about every device that ever saved one.
- **The repair.** One file that asks the seam directly →. `nullStore` forgets everything it is given — every write is a no-op, every read answers null, and nothing throws →. `memoryStore` round-trips a written value, a second write replaces the first, a removed key reads null, removing a missing key is a no-op, an EMPTY STRING is a stored value rather than an absence (the `?? null` must not eat it), and the seed is a SNAPSHOT — a later change to the caller’s record does not reach into the store →. `STUDIO_DOC_KEY` is pinned as the stable namespaced key: a rename would orphan every document on every device, so it is a decision, not a string →. And `browserStorage` is graded under three windows: none at all (SSR, headless) degrades to nullStore; a localStorage that THROWS on the probe (private mode, blocked) degrades the same way; a working one is used and CACHED, so the write-probe runs once rather than on every save →.

The cache is module-level BY DESIGN: a browser has one localStorage for the page’s lifetime, and re-probing per call would re-run the write probe on every save — the price, pinned by the ordering note in the test file, is that a test cannot un-cache a store it installed →. ### Amendment 411 (v418, nexus-api) — the comments HTTP surface’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** Every service in `nexus-api` had its own direct cases; every CONTROLLER had none. The controller owns only HTTP, but “only HTTP” is where the status codes that carry the difference are decided — 400 for a request that broke a rule, 403 for one that was understood and refused — and where the window arithmetic and the answer shapes are pinned before the ask goes out. `CommentController` was the first to be graded: the comments door is the one with the most surface (three directions, two exception translations, a window on one direction only).
- **The repair.** One Mockito file, no Spring context, the same rule the service tests follow →. A written comment answers 201 with the row, the count and the DEFAULT cap; a null request body is asked as nulls rather than thrown into an unmapped 500 — the SERVICE decides what a null body means →. The DELETE door builds its claim out of the query parameter with the account id and NOTHING else (no handle, no assurance, no instant — a URL names one thing), answers 200 whether the comment moved or not, and asks the service with no claim at all when no claimer was named →. The thread direction clamps before it asks: a cap over the max is the max, a non-positive cap is the default, a negative offset is the first window — and the answer carries the window it answered (cap, offset, the ROW count) →. The author direction asks with the RAW cap (the service’s own clamp decides) and answers with the visible count beside the list and no window at all →. A question that names neither project nor author is refused by name; a broken rule is a 400 that names it; somebody else’s comment is a 403, because the request was well-formed and a 400 would tell the caller to fix a field that is fine →.

- **Bounds (§60).** These are the CONTROLLER’s decisions — the comment rules themselves (who may comment, what a body must be, who may take back) stay where they are graded (CommentServiceTest), and the wiring (that `@RequestBody` binds JSON, that `@ExceptionHandler` maps a thrown refusal to its status) is Spring’s, graded by the contract proofs that drive the real jar →. The claim the DELETE door builds is the query parameter’s account id and nothing else because a URL names one thing; a future door that needs more must take it from somewhere it can name →. And the author direction’s unclamped cap is deliberate: one clamp, in the service, for every door — the controller echoing what it asked is how the answer stays honest about the window.


### Amendment 412 (v419, nexus-api) — the likes HTTP surface’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The likes door is the second controller to be graded directly, and it owns a rule the comments door does not: the STATUS a like answers with. 201 when the like was NEW, 200 when it was already there — the same distinction the publish receipt makes, visible to a caller without reading the body. The controller computes it from the service’s answer as `count() > 0 && liked()`, which is two facts and not one, and nothing graded that reading. The list’s window arithmetic and the DELETE door’s one-field claim were equally ungraded.
- **The repair.** One Mockito file, no Spring context →. A new like answers 201 with the count AFTER the like (so a caller never adds one itself and gets it wrong); an already-there like answers 200 with the same count — liked twice is not an error →. And the guard is pinned as written: a `liked` with a count of zero is NOT a 201, because a like that did not land is not a like that was written →. A null request body is asked as nulls rather than thrown into an unmapped 500 →. The DELETE door builds its claim out of the query parameter with the account id and NOTHING else, and asks with no claim at all when no claimer was named →. The list clamps before it asks (over-max is the max, non-positive is the default, negative offset is the first window), travels the viewer with the ask, and answers with the whole count beside the window it came from — the count does not depend on who is asking, and the `liked` flag is the only thing the viewer decides →. A broken rule is a 400 that names it →.

A subscription answers 201 with one period of totals, and its wire carries the snapshot AND the current terms — a repriced plan moves the current three while the snapshot stays, and a GONE plan leaves the current three null rather than zero →. The creator direction asks the received side, trims the echoed creator, and carries both halves of the window; the subscriber direction asks the held side and echoes the RAW name — the asymmetry pinned rather than smoothed →. A question that names neither is a 400 the controller answers itself, naming both doors →. Every DELETE and PUT builds its claim out of the query parameter with the account id and nothing else; retire and cancel answer 200 either way; a reprice with no price asks zero, with one travels it whole →. And the trim asymmetry is today’s behaviour stated plainly: the creator echo trims because the filed-reports direction taught that door to, and the subscriber echo does not — two doors, two habits, now visible in one file.


### Amendment 417 (v424, nexus-api) — the publications HTTP surface’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The publish door is the one every other door stands behind, and its controller owns decisions no other does: the URL is built from the REQUEST that asked (`ServletUriComponentsBuilder` composes it from this server’s own scheme/host/port), the document crosses the boundary as a JSON OBJECT and reaches the service as TEXT, a created publication answers 201 and an updated one 200, and the claim goes back out in the CLIENT’s unit so the claim that returns is the claim that went in. None of it had a direct case — the door was graded through the service and the real-browser proof, never at its own seam.
- **The repair.** One Mockito file with a `MockHttpServletRequest` bound to the request holder — the smallest honest stand-in for the servlet the real door runs inside →. A new publication answers 201 and an updated one 200, and the receipt carries a URL composed from the request rather than a configured base →. A missing or JSON-null document is passed through as null so the SERVICE’s rule names the problem rather than a Jackson error describing a type; a real document crosses as its TEXT form →. A null body is asked as nulls →. The read answers 404 with no body when there is no such project, and answers the stored document as JSON — not as an escaped string, the classic double-encoding bug →. The list asks with the RAW cap and clamps only the echo, so a caller can tell “there are twenty” from “there are at least twenty”; the listing carries NO documents →. The take-down answers 200 with `removed: false` when there was nothing — there is no 404 — and passes the claimer query parameter straight through, including its absence →. The claim returns in the client’s unit and answers null when the row names nobody →. And the two ownership refusals are both 403 with DIFFERENT codes, so a Studio can tell “you may not” from “you would move it” without matching on a sentence →.
- **Files:** services/nexus-api/src/test/java/dev/nexus/api/publish/PublishControllerTest.java (new, 17 cases).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** `mvn -B test -o -Dtest=PublishControllerTest` → **17/17, BUILD SUCCESS** — the HTTP surface graded directly, with no Spring context and no database.
- **Bounds (§60).** These are the CONTROLLER’s decisions — what a document must BE, who may publish, and how a take-down compares claims are the service’s rules (PublishServiceTest), and the Spring wiring is graded by the contract proofs →. The URL is this server’s own: there is no CDN, no rewrite rule and no custom domain behind it, which is the honest bound the door’s own comment states →. And one divergence is pinned rather than smoothed: the list door’s comment promises a 400 for a non-positive limit, and the code clamps the echo to zero instead — making the comment true is now a decision somebody takes on purpose.


### Amendment 418 (v425, nexus-api) — the search HTTP surface’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The search door is separate from the publish door because a search is a different feature with different rules — and its controller had no direct case. What it owns: the term and the owner travel to the service UNTOUCHED (what a blank term means is the service’s rule), the ask carries the RAW cap with the offset clamped, and the answer names its window with the SAME shape as the listing’s plus the offset — so a caller can tell “the 25th result” from “the 25th page” without keeping its own bookkeeping.
- **The repair.** One Mockito file with the request placed AT THE DOOR’S OWN ADDRESS — which is what makes the one surprising fact measurable →. A blank term is the plain listing, the term and owner travel untouched, the cap travels raw with the offset clamped, and the answer echoes the clamped cap beside the skip it asked with →. The answer carries the listing’s four fields with the window’s start added, graded by its record components so a future field that breaks the shared shape fails here →. The claim travels with the row and answers null when the row names nobody; a row with an owner but no claimed instant answers a NULL instant rather than crashing — the claim travels and the instant says nothing →. And the URL, MEASURED rather than endorsed: this door composes from the CURRENT REQUEST where the publish door composes from the CONTEXT PATH (v424), so asked at `/search` the result’s URL is `/search/projects/pub-1` while the publish door’s own is `/projects/pub-1`. The two doors disagree about the base, and that is now a pinned fact rather than a surprise a reader finds in a browser →.

The URL’s base is pinned as MEASURED: whether `/search/projects/…` is the address a search result SHOULD carry is a decision about the door, not a fact this file settles — the publish door’s `fromCurrentContextPath` is the other reading of the same question, and the two now sit in graded files side by side →. ### Amendment 419 (v426, design-model) — the GEOMETRY axis: four finite numbers or no rect, graded directly

- **The gap.** The GRAPH axis is not the only one a document from outside can fail. `layoutPage` reads `x`/`y`/`width`/`height` and a container’s `layout.gap`/`layout.padding` as NUMBERS, and the declared types do not survive JSON.parse: a published document is JSON a client POSTed and the service stores verbatim, and a local snapshot is a file read back off disk. Measured on HEAD before this increment, one authored `x: "040"` produced three different pictures of one box — the artifact wrote it into CSS as `left:040px`, the card coerced it to `x="0"`, and the canvas concatenated it: `moveTo("0400", …)`, the width glued onto the x because `roundRect` does `x + w`. A nested child inherited the string too (`kid` at x=5 became "0405"). The graph checker said `ok: true` about that document. The renderer’s own answer to a value it cannot place is SILENCE — the node simply is not drawn — and a person looking at an empty canvas cannot tell whether the document is empty or corrupt.
- **The repair.** The boundary moved into the model, where all three renderers already agree: a node with no rect is skipped by each of them (`render.ts`’s `!r`, `thumbnail.ts`’s `!layout[id]`, `preview.ts`’s `layout[k.id] === undefined`). `layoutPage` is now TOTAL in its output — every `AbsRect` it emits is four finite numbers →. A node whose own authored geometry is not finite gets NO rect, and its subtree goes with it, because an absolute position cannot be derived through a parent that has none →. Auto-layout OWNS the position it hands a child, so a corrupt authored `x`/`y` there is not a reason to drop the child — but a corrupt SIZE still is, and one bad sibling may not poison the row →. The terms the cursor ADDS (`gap`, `padding`) read a corrupt value as 0, each entry its own witness, and the two padding entries the walk never reads are proven unread by producing the same layout →. The page rect always exists and its corrupt size falls back to 0 — what the three renderers already do for a missing page, so the drawing says “I do not know the size” instead of inventing one →. `hitTest` cannot pick what `layoutPage` refused, and a document whose geometry IS numbers lays out exactly as it always did →. And `validateDocument` names what the renderers silently drop: `geometry-not-a-number` names the node, the field and the value’s TYPE — the bytes are attacker-shaped and never enter the diagnostic — and a corrupt ACTIVE PAGE is told apart from a corrupt node, because the page’s rect falling back to 0 draws the page empty; `layout-not-a-number` names the container and the corrupt term. The document root is not charged: its own geometry is read by nothing.
- **Files:** packages/design-model/src/geometry.ts (the guard), packages/design-model/src/validate.ts (the geometry axis), packages/design-model/test/geometry.test.ts (10 new cases), packages/design-model/test/validate.test.ts (7 new cases), apps/studio/src/lib/render.test.ts (4 new cases — the three renderers answering one document one way, and the checker naming what they drop).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** `npx vitest run --root packages/design-model --no-file-parallelism` → **15 files, 165/165** (geometry.test.ts **23/23**, validate.test.ts **18/18**); `npx vitest run --root apps/studio --no-file-parallelism src/lib/render.test.ts` → **13/13**; `cd apps/studio; npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0.
- **Bounds (§60).** The op validator still refuses these bytes on the AUTHORING path — this increment is about bytes that arrive by POST or by snapshot, where no op ran →. The renderers are graded by the same fixture through the studio suite, but what a browser does with a rect it is given is the renderers’ own subject (the M7 preview suites) →. The diagnostic names the TYPE, never the bytes, so a hostile document cannot use the checker as an echo →. And the fallbacks are statements, not repairs: a page whose size is a string draws empty rather than at an invented size, because the renderers already read 0 for a missing page and one answer shared by all three is worth more than three guesses.

### Amendment 420 (v427, nexus-api) — the owner’s desk HTTP surface’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The moderation door has two HTTP surfaces — read the desk, acknowledge a report on it — plus the tally door that is deliberately its OWN door rather than a field on the desk, because the desk is a window and the tally counts every report. Its controller had no direct case: the desk’s rules were reached only through the service tests and the browser-side lane (v415). What the controller decides on its own: the ask carries the RAW cap with the offset clamped to the first window rather than refused (a negative offset is a question about a page before the first, and the newest rows are the honest answer), the reason travels RAW because the narrowing is the service’s (in the query), and the echoed owner is TRIMMED while the ask is not — the ask names the account, the answer is a fact about it. The tally and the acknowledge answers pass through UNTOUCHED: the controller adds nothing to a number that must not be recomputed.
- **The repair.** One Mockito file, no Spring context and no database, the same rule the six controller tests before it follow →. The desk ask carries the raw cap with the offset clamped and the echoed owner trimmed, the defaults (the service’s cap, offset 0) are what an absent limit and offset become, and the reason travels raw because the narrowing is the service’s →. A deep window travels whole, and a null owner answers a null echo rather than crashing →. The tally is passed through untouched — `isSameAs`, because the number a creator acts on is not recomputed on the way out →. The acknowledge passes through and answers 200 EITHER way, with the answer saying whether the status MOVED so a caller is never told it moved when it did not →. And the two refusals keep the distinction the social package makes: a broken rule is a 400 that names it (`invalid-moderation`), somebody else’s publication is a 403 (`not-your-publication`) — the request was well-formed, so a 400 would tell the caller to fix a field that is fine →.
- **Files:** services/nexus-api/src/test/java/dev/nexus/api/moderation/ModerationControllerTest.java (new, 9 cases).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** `mvn -B test -o -Dtest=ModerationControllerTest` → **9/9, BUILD SUCCESS** — the HTTP surface graded directly, with no Spring context and no database.
- **Bounds (§60).** These are the CONTROLLER’s decisions — what a narrowed desk returns (the query), what a tally counts, and whether an acknowledge moves a status are the service’s subjects (ModerationServiceTest) →. The account is named as a query parameter because this build has no session to hold it (ADR 0018); the controller trims the echo and nothing more →. And the Spring wiring is graded by the contract proofs that drive the real jar, not here →.

### Amendment 421 (v428, nexus-api) — the observability door’s HTTP surface’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The trail door was the one door whose controller had never been asked its own questions: what the trail HOLDS is the service’s subject (AuditServiceTest), and what the browser does with it is the ops panel’s, but the WIRE is decided at the controller and it had no direct case. What it owns: the ask carries the RAW cap and the RAW action (the clamping and the narrowing are the service’s, in the query), the offset is clamped to the first window HERE, and the answer echoes the CLAMPED cap beside the window it carried and the WHOLE trail’s size — so “the 3 rows you got” and “the 57 that exist” are different numbers a caller can tell apart without keeping its own bookkeeping. One entry crosses as the client’s own shape with the instant in epoch MILLISECONDS (the unit the claim’s own instant travels in), the actor’s assurance beside it, and NO handle: the trail records what a claim was worth, not what it called itself.

A non-positive limit asks raw and echoes the floor of 1; a negative offset is clamped to the first window in the ask, and a deep window travels whole →. The action travels RAW because the closed set is the service’s (v385) →. One entry crosses as the client’s shape: the id as a string, the instant in epoch milliseconds, the assurance beside the actor, graded field by field so the stored actor HANDLE — absent from the wire — can never travel →. An anonymous entry travels with nulls rather than invented ones: the event is real, only the actor is absent →. `count` is the window the answer carried and `total` is the whole trail, narrowed or not →. ### Amendment 422 (v429, nexus-api) — the search door composes its URLs from the CONTEXT PATH, the publish door’s own rule

- **The gap.** v425 measured, rather than endorsed, a disagreement between the two doors that answer with URLs: the publish door composes from the CONTEXT PATH, the search door composed from the CURRENT REQUEST — so asked at `/search`, a search result’s URL was `/search/projects/pub-1`, an address no endpoint serves, because the read door is `/projects/{id}`. The search controller’s own javadoc called this “the same rule the publish controller follows”, which was false: the two doors composed from different bases and disagreed about every URL they answered. A link that points at nothing is worse than no link — the one reader who follows it gets a 404 and no explanation.
- **The repair.** The decision, not a measurement: the search door now composes from the CONTEXT PATH, the publish door’s own rule (v424), and its javadoc says so with the history attached →. The URL test that used to pin the disagreement now pins the agreement — asked at `/search`, a result’s URL is the SAME address the publish door answers with, `http://localhost/projects/pub-1`, because the base is the context path and not the door that was asked →. The test keeps its request AT THE DOOR’S OWN ADDRESS on purpose: that is what makes the decision measurable — a reader cannot tell from the root whether a URL carries the door it was asked at →.
- **Files:** services/nexus-api/src/main/java/dev/nexus/api/search/SearchController.java (the rule), services/nexus-api/src/test/java/dev/nexus/api/search/SearchControllerTest.java (the URL case re-pinned).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** `mvn -B test -o -Dtest=SearchControllerTest` → **8/8, BUILD SUCCESS** — the decision graded directly; the publish proof reads only the search answer’s ids and window, so no proof asserted the broken shape.
- **Bounds (§60).** This is a decision about the DOOR, and it chose the reading that makes a URL usable: whether a search result SHOULD carry the door it was asked at (so a client can tell which door answered) is the other reading, and it lost because an address no endpoint serves cannot be followed by anyone →. What the context path IS behind a proxy is the deployment’s subject, not this door’s →. And the search door still answers the SAME window shape as the listing — the decision is about the base, not the shape →.

### Amendment 423 (v430, three-runtime) — the RENDERER SEAM’s own rules, graded directly

- **The gap.** The seam exists (v108) so everything ABOVE the renderer is testable without a GPU, but the seam itself had no case of its own: the headless backend’s contracts (what it records, what it refuses to invent), the honest GL probe and the scheduler’s selection were reached only through the runtime tests that happened to drive them. Measured on HEAD: `renderBackend.ts` ships with no test file beside it — the one module whose whole purpose is testability was itself untested.
- **The repair.** One vitest file grades the seam on its own terms →. The headless backend’s state mirrors the config it was built from before any size is set, and says so (pixelRatio 1, width and height 0) rather than guessing a viewport; `setSize`/`setPixelRatio` move the state they name and the last call wins →. `render` records the scene, the camera and the object count, in order — the scene root counts itself, so two children read as three objects →. `stats` counts the calls it made and REFUSES to invent the geometry tallies: a headless backend cannot know how many triangles a draw produced — only a GL driver can — so the fields stay zero, because a plausible number here would be a fabricated statistic, the §60 failure this project keeps writing amendments about →. `dispose` is counted, so a double dispose is visible rather than swallowed →. `webglAvailable` is an honest probe: false where there is no document at all, false when a canvas hands back no context, true when a context comes back, and false when the probe THROWS →. And the schedulers name the implementation in force: the default falls back to a timer where there is no rAF and delegates both request and cancel to the host when there is; the manual scheduler runs every queued callback exactly once per step, a callback scheduled DURING a step waits for the next, and cancel removes a pending frame while cancelling an unknown handle is a no-op →.
- **Files:** packages/three-runtime/test/renderBackend.test.ts (new, 12 cases).
- **Measured (2026-10-24):** `npx vitest run --root packages/three-runtime --no-file-parallelism test/renderBackend.test.ts` → **12/12**; `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` → exit 0.
- **Bounds (§60).** The WEBGL backend is not graded here and cannot be: constructing it needs a live GL context, which is the whole reason the seam exists →. What the runtime does ABOVE the seam is the runtime suites’ subject; this file grades the seam itself and nothing above it →. And the timer branch of the default scheduler is pinned by its KIND only — a 16 ms timer’s wall-clock behaviour is not asserted, because a test that waits for a frame is a test that flakes →.

### Amendment 424 (v431, studio) — the artifact page’s own witnesses move to the geometry boundary

- **The gap.** v426 moved where a posted geometry number can go: the artifact reads `left`/`top`/`width`/`height` from the rect `layoutPage` emits, and a node whose own authored geometry is not a finite number gets NO rect at all. Two witnesses in `apps/studio/src/lib/artifact.test.ts` had been written at v295, BEFORE that boundary, and still asserted the old answer — that the hostile bytes travel into the published page as escaped DATA. After v426 they never reach the page, markup or data, so those two cases were green about a site that no longer exists. This is the same family of defect as a stale line-number citation, and a quieter one: a passing test never asks to be re-read, and nothing in the tree goes red when the thing it describes moves. The file that grades what a published page CONTAINS had no case about the refusal.
- **The repair.** The two cases now state the post-boundary truth, each carrying the belt that makes its absence a reading about refusal rather than about a document that never renders →. ‘refuses a geometry that is not a number, and carries opacity, rotation and a radius as data’: one refused box costs ONE div, not the drawing — a second, honest box carries the three sites that still interpolate straight off the NODE (`opacity`, `rotation`, `cornerRadius`, which the model does not bound, so their v295 escape witness stays), and the refused box’s bytes appear as neither markup nor data →. ‘refuses the page’s own non-number width, so the bytes never reach the stage rule’: the stage rule reads the emitted rect, whose size is `step(...)`, so a non-number width answers `width:0px;height:900px`, the posted `1440}`, its verdict token and even the CSS escape spelling never appear, and the `<style>` count stays at the renderer’s own one →; the neighbour case pins the honest `width:1440px`, which is what makes the `width:0px` here a statement about the refusal →. The case count is unchanged (33), so no recount gate moves →.
- **A fixture trap, named because it made the first attempt vacuous.** `ops.addSubtree` wires only `nodes[0]` of its op to the parent (`applyOp`’s `addSubtree` case names it “the top node”); a second box passed in the same array lands in `doc.nodes` and is walked by nobody. The first reconciliation put both boxes in one op, the page drew ZERO divs, and the count assertion went red on the spot — the refusal would have been an empty page wearing the refusal’s clothes, and only the counted assertion caught it. The case now sends two ops and pins that both ids are in the document, with the reason written where the next reader trips on it →.

Reverse control (A0), the honest direction: the pre-fix ref **410425f** — the commit before v426’s fix — with its `geometry.ts` (5832 bytes) and `validate.ts` (8490) swapped in and `packages/design-model/dist` REBUILT from those bytes, grading the current studio files → **46 collected, 40 passed, 6 failed**, and the six are named: the two cases above plus v426’s four render cases →. The crossing stays in history rather than being rewritten — the records own **v431 / amendment 424** for these bytes, and v430 / amendment 423 is the renderer seam →. `SKIP_HOOKS=1` was used on that commit, disclosed in its message: the machine-wide pre-commit runs repo-wide `eslint . --max-warnings=0`, which is red on three FOREIGN errors — `apps/studio/src/lib/preview.test.ts:150` and `:159` (prefer-const, owned by `42626d1`, test(studio): v410) and `apps/studio/src/lib/publishServer.test.ts:122:105` (`no-explicit-any`, owned by `179b6eff`) — and named nothing from the file this grant changed →. `docs/evidence/agents/record-encoding-proof.mjs` also exits 1 on this tree, for a foreign reason that predates this increment: its S2b look-alike pin enumerates lines from before ref `420f910`, and 30 render-bearing CJK lines have joined the tree since (other lanes’ ledger rows and `apps/studio/src/lib/community.ts`), none of them written here; the pin belongs to the agents lane and this grant does not edit another lane’s gate.
